entries.title: Slow Zoom In
entries.text:
Slow Zoom In

gradual zoomcreep zoomCreeping zoomZoom progressif

A slow zoom in is slow zoom in cinematography that tightens the frame by increasing focal length while the camera body stays locked. Perspective relations stay fixed: the world does not slide, it only enlarges as the lens compresses space.

Volume

Create this Slow Zoom In

Narrative function

The shot is a thought that closes without walking. Geography stays put, so the audience feels watched or analyzed rather than approached.

Faces grow, walls stay in the same relation, and the pressure is optical. Use it when attention must narrow and the room must not rearrange itself.

It is the wrong tool when you need to enter a mind by occupying the same air: that job belongs to a physical approach, because a zoom never changes the camera's station point.

How it works

Lock a heavy tripod. Keep height, tilt, and nodal point still.

Drive focal length smoothly over several seconds and rehearse focus compensation as depth of field shallows. Compression increases: distant planes look closer to the subject even though nobody moved.

Prompt a locked camera body, a gradual optical zoom in, rising compression, and an explicit ban on dolly parallax.

When to use it

Use it to raise pressure on a still figure while the architecture stays legally the same. Concrete beat: a surveillance long-lens slowly isolating one person in a crowd.

Do not use it if foreground objects must peel and prove the camera walked.

Compared with similar shots

A Dolly In translates the whole camera, so foreground and background change speed. A Push In is a physical or virtual walk whose job is a realization landing.

A Crash Zoom In uses the same optical mechanism at sting speed. Stay on slow zoom in when the station point must not move.

Push InA thought lands. Do not rush it.

Dolly InEnter a mind, a room, or a threat. Geography changes because the camera walks.

Crash Zoom InPunctuate a hit, a realization, or a comic sting.

In film

The Conversation isolates figures in Union Square with a gradual long-lens close. There Will Be Blood and Phantom Thread use slow optical tightening as patience and scrutiny.

These are grammar for locked-body compression, not frames to copy.

Barry Lyndon 1975Slow widening views reveal painterly social tableaux.

The Conversation 1974The opening surveillance view gradually isolates figures in Union Square.

Prompt it

Slow optical zoom in on [Subject], camera body locked on a heavy tripod, lens gradually tightening over several seconds, background compression increasing, no physical dolly, prestige-drama patience. For motion: the lens slowly zooms in for 6 seconds while the camera body stays locked and the subject stays centered.

Smooth optical zoom only.

Use in Video Generator

From a distant fixed window, slowly zoom into a solitary woman waiting at the center of a city square. Eight seconds, no camera translation, no foreground parallax, patient observational mood. She never acknowledges the camera.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Dolly In or a digital crop sold as a zoom. The tell is parallax: if a foreground chair slides against the wall, you translated.

The fix is a locked head, a true focal-length change, and a hold on the final tight frame.

Questions

What is Slow Zoom In in film?

It is a gradual increase of focal length with the camera support still. The image tightens and space compresses, but the camera does not occupy a new position.

Slow Zoom In vs Dolly In

Dolly in walks the camera so perspective and parallax change. Slow zoom in only walks the lens: size grows, relative geometry of planes stays the same.

When should I use Slow Zoom In?

When you want pressure, scrutiny, or a slow isolation and you need the room to remain the same place. Skip it if the beat is actually entering the space.

How do I prompt Slow Zoom In for AI image or video?

Name a locked tripod, optical zoom in, duration, and no body travel. Example: camera body locked, lens slowly zooming in for 6 seconds, compression increasing, no dolly.

entries.title: Slow Zoom Out
entries.text:
Slow Zoom Out

A slow zoom out widens the frame by decreasing focal length while the support stays put. More architecture and negative space enter the picture, yet the camera never travels, so true parallax does not appear.

Volume

Create this Slow Zoom Out

Narrative function

The joke, the trap, or the social system was already around the person. The lens simply admits it.

Because the station point is unchanged, the reveal feels observational: we were always this far away, we only chose to see more. It is the wrong tool when the camera must retreat through a doorway, lose a foreground, or leave someone behind in real space.

Optical widening cannot walk out of a room.

How it works

Lock the tripod and reverse the zoom. Start on a composed tight frame and pre-compose the wide end so heads, signs, and negative space land.

Focus will deepen as focal length shortens. Prompt a tripod-locked optical zoom out, no camera body travel, and name what architecture must appear by the last frame.

When to use it

Use it to reveal context, isolation, or an off-screen joke that was already in the location. Concrete beat: a tight face opening onto a dinner table that has been watching.

Do not use it to exit a location: that is a physical pull.

Compared with similar shots

A Pull Out and a Dolly Out move the camera backward, so foreground objects leave the frame with parallax. A slow zoom out only changes the lens angle of view.

If you also need a Slow Zoom In cousin in the same scene, keep both bodies locked so the pair stays optical.

Pull OutShow the container around a feeling.

Dolly OutLeave someone behind, or show how small they are in the system.

Slow Zoom InUse to raise pressure without changing geography. The world stays put; attention closes.

In film

Barry Lyndon widens into painterly social tableaux without walking the camera into the party. The Social Network, Her, and Lost in Translation use slow optical opening to place a person inside a system they cannot leave.

Grammar, not frames to copy.

Prompt it

Slow optical zoom out from [Subject], tripod locked, the frame breathing open to reveal surrounding architecture and negative space, no camera body travel. For motion: the lens slowly zooms out for 6 seconds from a tight frame on [Subject] into a wider environment.

Camera body stays still.

Use in Video Generator

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Dolly Out. The tell is a sliding foreground: plants, shoulders, or door jambs changing their overlap.

The fix is to freeze the support and drive only focal length, then hold the wide.

Questions

What is Slow Zoom Out in film?

It is a gradual decrease of focal length from a locked camera, so the frame widens while the camera's position stays the same.

Slow Zoom Out vs Dolly Out

Dolly out retreats through space and creates parallax. Slow zoom out stays on the sticks and only widens the lens, so planes keep their original perspective relation.

When should I use Slow Zoom Out?

When the surrounding situation is the punchline or the prison, and you want to disclose it without relocating the camera. Do not use it as a substitute for leaving the room.

How do I prompt Slow Zoom Out for AI image or video?

State locked tripod, optical zoom out, and what must be revealed. Example: tripod locked, lens slowly zooming out for 6 seconds, architecture entering, no body travel.

entries.title: Crash Zoom In
entries.text:
Crash Zoom In

whip zoomsnap zoomzoom inzoom outslow zoomZoom coup de poing

A crash zoom is a rapid focal-length snap from a wider frame into a detail, usually without moving the camera. The punch is optical and conspicuous: size changes faster than a body can walk.

Volume

Create this Crash Zoom In

Narrative function

The shot punctuates a hit, a name, a weapon, or a comic sting. Artificiality is the point.

The audience is not invited to approach; they are struck by a lens. It is the wrong tool for a thought that should land over several seconds, and the wrong tool for geography.

After the snap, hold. If you keep zooming or add shake, the sting becomes noise.

How it works

Keep the subject on the zoom center. Use a controlled fast zoom or, in post, a high-resolution crop that still behaves like optics, not a warp.

Expect radial motion blur during the snap, then a hard hold on the tight frame. Avoid autofocus hunting.

Prompt an aggressive optical punch-in under one second, zoom blur, then a locked tight hold, and ban a physical dolly.

When to use it

Use it to punctuate a hit, a realization, or a comic sting. Concrete beat: a name is spoken and the face slams into close-up.

Do not use it as a substitute for walking closer through a room.

Compared with similar shots

A Slow Zoom In is the same optical family at patience speed. A Dolly In has parallax and feels like a person stepping in.

A Whip Pan blurs by rotating the head, not by changing focal length. Crash zoom in is a snap of the lens, then a hold.

Crash Zoom OutShock-reveal scale or undercut a close moment.

Whip PanTransition, punchline, or sudden attention shift.

Slow Zoom InUse to raise pressure without changing geography. The world stays put; attention closes.

In film

Django Unchained uses abrupt zooms as Western punctuation. The Grand Budapest Hotel snaps to comic information.

Kill Bill and Hot Fuzz treat the crash zoom as genre grammar rather than invisibility. Use the speed and the hold, not the costumes.

Django Unchained 2012Abrupt zooms punctuate reactions and Western-style confrontations.

The Grand Budapest Hotel 2014Sudden reframings emphasize comic information.

Prompt it

Aggressive crash zoom into [Subject], snap optical punch-in under one second, radial motion blur, Shaw Brothers energy, then a hard hold on the tight frame. For motion: sudden crash zoom into [Subject] in under a second, then hold.

Heavy zoom blur during the snap.

Use in Video Generator

A solemn auctioneer lifts a plain wooden box. Snap-zoom instantly from a medium shot to the tiny blinking light hidden under its lid. Fixed camera position, strong punchy zoom, immediate sharp landing, no forward dolly and no slow-motion.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a fast Dolly In or a Whip Pan. The tell is parallax or horizontal streaking instead of radial zoom blur.

The fix: camera body still, subject on center, snap, then freeze the tight frame. Do not add unrelated camera shake.

Questions

What is Crash Zoom In in film?

It is a very fast increase of focal length that slams from a wider shot into a detail, usually from a locked camera, then holds.

Crash Zoom In vs Dolly In

Dolly in moves the camera through space. Crash zoom in changes only the lens, often with radial blur, and reads as a punctuation mark rather than an approach.

When should I use Crash Zoom In?

When a fact must hit: a face, a gun, a title, a joke. Use it once per beat and hold. Do not use it to tour a location.

How do I prompt Crash Zoom In for AI image or video?

Demand a snap optical zoom in under one second, radial zoom blur, a still camera body, and a hard hold. Ban dolly and extra shake.

entries.title: Crash Zoom Out
entries.text:
Crash Zoom Out

A crash zoom out is a sudden, fast widening of the lens from a tight frame into a much wider one, usually without moving the camera. It dumps the subject back into the environment in a fraction of a second.

Volume

Create this Crash Zoom Out

Narrative function

Scale, danger, or a joke appears all at once. The close moment is undercut because the world was always that large; the lens simply confessed.

The snap is the comedy or the horror, not a polite reveal. It is the wrong tool when you need to walk backward through furniture, or when the newly revealed space must pass the camera in layers.

Optical dump is not a retreat.

How it works

Lock the body. Center the zoom so the subject does not smear sideways.

Snap from the tight composition to a pre-composed wide in under a second, then hold the wide. Radial blur during the change, not handheld bounce.

Prompt a sudden crash zoom out, environment exploding into view, then a locked wide hold.

When to use it

Use it to shock-reveal scale or undercut a close moment. Concrete beat: an intimate two-shot snaps to a parking lot full of witnesses.

Do not use it when the camera must physically leave the subject.

Compared with similar shots

A Crash Zoom In punches the other way, into a detail. A Pull Out translates the camera backward with parallax.

A Slow Zoom Out discloses the same optical widening without the sting. Crash zoom out is the dump, then the hold.

Crash Zoom InPunctuate a hit, a realization, or a comic sting.

Pull OutShow the container around a feeling.

Slow Zoom InUse to raise pressure without changing geography. The world stays put; attention closes.

In film

Shaun of the Dead snaps from faces into wider comic geography. Evil Dead uses violent optical widening as shock.

Hot Fuzz works the same family in both directions. Copy the snap-and-hold, not the gag content.

Prompt it

Sudden crash zoom out from [Subject], the environment exploding into view in a fraction of a second, then a locked wide hold. For motion: snap zoom out from [Subject] in under a second, revealing the wider scene, then hold.

Use in Video Generator

Snap zoom out from [Subject] in under a second, revealing the wider scene, then hold.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Dolly Out or a Crash Zoom In fired in the wrong direction. The tell is sliding foreground or a punch that gets tighter instead of wider.

The fix: locked body, pre-composed wide end, snap out, hold.

Questions

What is Crash Zoom Out in film?

It is a very fast decrease of focal length that throws a tight image into a wide one, usually from a still camera, then holds the wide.

Crash Zoom Out vs Pull Out

A pull out moves the camera away so space opens with parallax. A crash zoom out only widens the lens, so the station point never changes.

When should I use Crash Zoom Out?

When you need an instant scale joke, a threat revealed around a close face, or a hard undercut. Do not use it as a slow exit.

How do I prompt Crash Zoom Out for AI image or video?

Write snap zoom out in under a second, camera body still, environment appearing at once, then a locked wide hold. Ban physical retreat.

Melies is the AI filmmaking workspace. This Crash Zoom Out opens with the camera path and prompt already loaded, so you generate the move instead of describing it from scratch.

entries.title: Dolly In
entries.text:
Dolly In

truck indolly forwardDolly shotdolly outlateral dollydiagonal dollyPush-inTravelling avant

A dolly in shot moves the entire camera through space on a wheeled or tracked support, advancing toward the subject at a measured pace. The nodal point walks, so foreground and background shift in parallax as the surroundings are progressively excluded.

Volume

Create this Dolly In

Narrative function

The camera enters a mind, a room, or a threat by occupying new air. Unlike a cut, the audience experiences the change of attention continuously.

A small travel can make a thought feel consequential because space itself has agreed to close. It is the wrong tool when you want optical compression without new geography, or when the beat is only a sting.

If the track is longer than the thought, the move tours.

How it works

Lay track or roll a wheeled dolly on a known axis. Fix focal length, usually a moderate spherical such as 40mm.

Keep eye height constant unless the story changes rank. Tie the arrival at close-up to a change in the actor's thought.

Foreground objects will slide. Prompt a physical dolly in on track, camera body gliding forward, parallax shifting, no optical zoom.

When to use it

Use it to enter a mind, a room, or a threat, because geography changes when the camera walks. Concrete beat: a medium two-shot that arrives on a lie forming in one face.

Do not use a digital zoom and call it a dolly.

Compared with similar shots

A Slow Zoom In keeps the station point and only changes focal length, so there is no walking parallax. A Push In is the pressure job that can be a short dolly, slider, or Steadicam; dolly in names the wheeled path and the traction.

Tracking Shot matches a mover instead of closing on a still thought.

Push InA thought lands. Do not rush it.

Slow Zoom InUse to raise pressure without changing geography. The world stays put; attention closes.

Tracking ShotAccompany a walker. The shot is a journey, not a picture.

In film

The Shining uses measured forward travel through the hotel so rooms become traps. Goodfellas often walks the camera as social pressure, distinct from its Copa track.

Oldboy's corridor work is mostly lateral tracking; use it as a reminder that forward dolly and side track are different axes. Grammar for translation, not a shot to duplicate.

Jaws 1975The gradual approach toward Quint during the Indianapolis monologue; shot boundaries and camera-versus-zoom mechanics require an edition check.

Prompt it

Physical dolly in toward [Subject] on track, camera body gliding forward, parallax shifting foreground against background, 40mm spherical, buttery traction. For motion: the camera physically dollies forward toward [Subject] for 6 seconds.

Foreground parallax, no optical zoom.

Use in Video Generator

An archivist sits at a desk and notices a familiar signature on an old letter. Begin in a medium-wide shot. Over eight seconds dolly slowly forward to a close-up, fixed lens, subtle foreground parallax, no zoom. Her eyes lift only at the end. Restrained daylight, no cut.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Slow Zoom In or a crop. The tell is missing parallax: walls grow but never slide.

The fix is a real translation, fixed focal length, constant eye height, and an end frame tied to a thought, not to a clock.

Questions

What is Dolly In in film?

It is a physical advance of the camera on wheels or track toward a subject, changing perspective and introducing parallax as the frame tightens.

Dolly In vs Slow Zoom In

Slow zoom in enlarges from a locked position and compresses space. Dolly in walks the camera, so near objects move faster than far ones and the room rearranges.

When should I use Dolly In?

When a thought, a threat, or a room must be entered in continuous space. Do not use it for a one-frame sting or for a lens-only squeeze.

How do I prompt Dolly In for AI image or video?

Say physical dolly in on track, fixed lens, forward body travel, visible foreground parallax, no optical zoom. Name the start size and the arrival size.

entries.title: Dolly Out
entries.text:
Dolly Out

truck outpull backDolly shotdolly inlateral dollydiagonal dollyPull-back revealTravelling arrière

A dolly out shot withdraws the entire camera through space on a wheeled or tracked support. The world widens with true parallax, and the subject shrinks inside architecture because the station point has actually retreated.

Volume

Create this Dolly Out

Narrative function

We understand an expression first, then discover the social situation or danger that gives it meaning. Leaving someone behind is a spatial fact: the camera walks away, so the person is abandoned in a real room.

It is the wrong tool when you only need a detached, flat widening, or when the famous pull-back you remember was actually a zoom. Check perspective before you name the rig.

How it works

Compose the tight and wide endpoints first. Reveal surrounding elements in a deliberate order as the dolly retreats.

Keep focal length fixed so size change comes from distance. Foreground will enter from the edges.

Prompt a physical dolly out on track, true parallax, subject shrinking inside architecture, no zoom-out.

When to use it

Use it to leave someone behind, or to show how small they are in the system. Concrete beat: a confession in close coverage, then the camera retreats until the office owns them.

Do not call every famous pull-back a dolly.

Compared with similar shots

A Pull Out is the generic retreat job and may be virtual, Steadicam, or crane-backed; dolly out specifies wheeled translation at human height. A Slow Zoom Out widens without walking.

An Aerial Pullback leaves the ground and hands the scene to geography from above.

Pull OutShow the container around a feeling.

Aerial PullbackClose a chapter. Geography wins.

Slow Zoom InUse to raise pressure without changing geography. The world stays put; attention closes.

In film

A Clockwork Orange withdraws from Alex to reveal the Korova Milk Bar. The Godfather opens by withdrawing from Bonasera until the office encounter is the room.

The Truman Show uses retreat to disclose the container around a life. Confirm each shot's parallax before treating it as track.

A Clockwork Orange 1971Opening withdrawal from Alex to reveal the Korova Milk Bar.

The Godfather 1972Opening withdrawal from Bonasera reveals the office encounter.

Prompt it

Physical dolly out from [Subject], camera retreating on track, the world widening with true parallax, subject shrinking inside architecture. For motion: the camera physically dollies backward away from [Subject], revealing more environment with parallax.

Use in Video Generator

Start tightly on a calm pianist’s face. Pull the camera backward in one uninterrupted shot, fixed focal length, gradually revealing that the grand piano stands alone in a flooded ballroom. Keep the face natural and delay the water reveal until the middle of the shot.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Slow Zoom Out. The tell is a flat grow of the frame with no new overlap of furniture.

The fix: translate backward, keep the lens fixed, and let foreground objects arrive at the edges in order.

Questions

What is Dolly Out in film?

It is a physical retreat of the camera on wheels or track, opening space around a subject with changing perspective and parallax.

Dolly Out vs Slow Zoom Out

Slow zoom out stays put and only widens the lens. Dolly out moves the camera backward, so the room's layers slide and the person is left in real space.

When should I use Dolly Out?

When isolation, abandonment, or a revealed system must be walked, not merely disclosed by the lens. Do not use it for a sting widen.

How do I prompt Dolly Out for AI image or video?

Write physical dolly backward on track, fixed focal length, parallax, subject shrinking in architecture. Ban optical zoom out.

entries.title: Dolly Left
entries.text:
Dolly Left

truck left

A dolly left, also called a truck left, slides the whole camera sideways to the left on wheels or track. The lens stays aimed with the subject while background planes peel past in parallax.

Volume

Create this Dolly Left

Narrative function

The shot surveys a space or stays with a walker without yawing the head. New information enters from the left as the right side of the room exits.

Because the camera translates, pillars and furniture change their overlap instead of merely sweeping. It is the wrong tool when you only need to look left from a locked tripod.

A pan would rotate; this move relocates.

How it works

Lay track parallel to the action, horizon locked, height constant. Do not pan to invent the move: the body slides, the lens holds its relative aim.

Subject may stay framed while the world peels, or the camera may discover a new person as it trucks. Prompt a lateral dolly left on track, background planes peeling, subject tracked in frame.

When to use it

Use it to survey a space or stay with a walker without turning the camera. Concrete beat: sliding along a diner counter so each stool and face arrives in order.

Do not pan from sticks and label it a truck.

Compared with similar shots

A Pan Left rotates on a fixed vertical axis with no body travel. A Dolly Right is the same translation the other way: pick the direction that reveals new information.

Tracking Shot often trucks like this while matching a mover's pace; dolly left can also survey a still line of objects.

Dolly RightOpposite of dolly left; pick the direction that reveals new information.

Tracking ShotAccompany a walker. The shot is a journey, not a picture.

Slow Zoom InUse to raise pressure without changing geography. The world stays put; attention closes.

In film

There Will Be Blood uses lateral travel to read rooms and landscapes as systems. In the Mood for Love slides along corridors and walls so delay and gossip live in the peeling planes.

Use the side-slip, not the color grade.

Prompt it

Lateral dolly left across [Subject], camera sliding sideways on track, background planes peeling in parallax, subject tracked in frame. For motion: the camera slides left on a dolly, keeping [Subject] in frame, background parallax visible.

Use in Video Generator

The camera slides left on a dolly, keeping [Subject] in frame, background parallax visible.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Pan Left. The tell is a rotating horizon of objects with no change of station point, and no peeling of near columns against far walls.

The fix is a true sideways translation, level horizon, fixed height.

Questions

What is Dolly Left in film?

It is a lateral truck of the camera body to the left on wheels or track, keeping the lens aimed while space peels in parallax.

Dolly Left vs Pan Left

Pan left turns the head on a locked tripod. Dolly left moves the support sideways, so foreground and background slide at different speeds.

When should I use Dolly Left?

When the next fact is to the left in real space and you want to arrive there by traveling, not by looking. Do not use it if a simple pan connects the two facts.

How do I prompt Dolly Left for AI image or video?

Specify lateral dolly left on track, no pan, locked horizon, visible parallax, subject held in frame. Name what new architecture enters from the left.

entries.title: Dolly Right
entries.text:
Dolly Right

truck right

A dolly right, or truck right, moves the camera body sideways to the right without panning. New space enters from one side of the frame while the other side exits, and layered parallax proves the translation.

Volume

Create this Dolly Right

Narrative function

Direction is a reveal order. Trucking right can disclose a listener, a door, or a threat that was legally off-screen to camera right.

The horizon stays level; only the world slides. It is the wrong tool when the camera should yaw to glance, or when a few centimeters of slider would be enough.

Pick the side that produces information, not a decorative glide.

How it works

Track parallel, height and tilt constant, no compensatory pan unless you are combining moves on purpose. Keep the horizon locked.

Prompt a lateral dolly right, smooth sideways travel, layered parallax, locked horizon.

When to use it

Use the opposite of dolly left: pick the direction that reveals new information. Concrete beat: sliding right along a car's profile until a second passenger appears.

Do not truck both ways in one clip without a reason.

Compared with similar shots

Dolly Left is the same physics mirrored. A Pan Right only rotates.

Tracking Shot uses this lateral axis when the subject is also moving; dolly right can scan a still lineup. A Slider Shot is a short version of the same linear idea.

Dolly LeftSurvey a space or stay with a walker without turning the camera.

Tracking ShotAccompany a walker. The shot is a journey, not a picture.

Slow Zoom InUse to raise pressure without changing geography. The world stays put; attention closes.

In film

Children of Men often relocates the camera through real streets rather than glancing from a locked head. The Player's studio-lot sentence includes lateral travel as part of a longer choreography.

Take the side-slip as grammar, not the whole oner.

Prompt it

Lateral dolly right across [Subject], smooth sideways travel, layered parallax, locked horizon. For motion: the camera slides right on a dolly, keeping [Subject] framed, smooth lateral parallax.

Use in Video Generator

The camera slides right on a dolly, keeping [Subject] framed, smooth lateral parallax.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Pan Right or an 360-Degree Orbit that starts to curve. The tell is yaw, a dipping horizon, or a changing camera-to-subject distance.

The fix: straight track, rightward translation, constant radius to the subject if you are holding them.

Questions

What is Dolly Right in film?

It is a sideways translation of the camera to the right on wheels or track, with the lens holding its aim and the background peeling in parallax.

Dolly Right vs Pan Right

Pan right is rotation from a fixed support. Dolly right relocates the support, so near objects pass faster than distant ones.

When should I use Dolly Right?

When the story fact you need is to camera right and should be reached by travel. Do not use it as a default polish on a lock-off.

How do I prompt Dolly Right for AI image or video?

Write dolly right on track, no pan, locked horizon, layered parallax, subject kept in frame. State what enters from the right.

A pan left is pan shot cinematography that rotates the camera on a fixed tripod or head around its vertical axis, sweeping the view to the left. The support does not travel; only the direction of the lens changes.

Volume

Create this Pan Left

Narrative function

Two facts in one geography get connected by a look. A rider and a doorway, a speaker and the person they will not face.

Because the sticks stay put, the audience remains in one station and is asked only to turn. It is the wrong tool when you must pass behind a column with true parallax, or when the blur of a whip is the point.

If foreground does not need to slide, a pan is enough. If it does, truck.

How it works

Level the horizon on a fluid head. Rotate yaw only.

Start and end on composed frames, feather the start and stop, and keep the nodal point over the tripod so the pan does not walk. No body travel.

Prompt a slow pan left from a locked tripod, rotation on the vertical axis, level horizon, new architecture to the left.

When to use it

Use it to connect two things in one geography without moving the support. Concrete beat: a look off left, then the pan finds what they see.

Do not tour a whole room if a cut or a track would be cleaner.

Compared with similar shots

A Dolly Left translates and peels planes. A Pan Right is the same rotation the other way.

A Whip Pan is this axis past the blur threshold, often used as a join. A Tilt Up rotates on the horizontal axis instead.

Pan RightSame as pan left, other direction. End on the story beat.

Whip PanTransition, punchline, or sudden attention shift.

Tilt UpReveal height, awe, or a face last.

In film

The Searchers connects rider, land, and doorway with turning looks from a held position. The Rules of the Game (on the sister page as a right pan) is the same Renoir law: a head turn through deep space.

Weekend is often listed beside long connecting moves; confirm whether a given beat is a pan or a lateral track before copying its mechanism.

Prompt it

Slow pan left from a locked tripod across [Subject], camera rotating on its vertical axis, horizon level, revealing new architecture to the left. For motion: the camera pans left from a fixed tripod, sweeping across [Subject] and the environment.

No body travel.

Use in Video Generator

The camera pans left from a fixed tripod, sweeping across [Subject] and the environment. No body travel.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Dolly Left. The tell is missing parallax of near objects, or the opposite: you added a slide by accident.

The fix: freeze the tripod position, yaw left, level horizon, composed start and end.

Questions

What is Pan Left in film?

It is a leftward rotation of a camera on a locked support around the vertical axis, changing where the lens points without relocating the tripod.

Pan Left vs Dolly Left

Dolly left moves the camera sideways through space. Pan left only turns the head, so perspective from the station point stays the same.

When should I use Pan Left?

When two facts share a geography and a turn of attention is enough. Do not pan if you need to physically pass objects in depth.

How do I prompt Pan Left for AI image or video?

Say locked tripod, pan left, vertical-axis rotation only, level horizon, no body travel. Name the start subject and what is revealed to the left.

entries.title: Pan Right
entries.text:
Pan Right

A pan right shot is a horizontal rotation of a locked-off camera toward the right. It connects two parts of the same geography in one continuous turn from a single station point.

Volume

Create this Pan Right

Narrative function

End on the story beat, not on a wall. The rightward turn can follow a look, a car, or a line of dialogue that points off-screen.

Because the camera does not walk, the ethics of the shot stay those of a witness who can turn but cannot follow. It is the wrong tool for a chase that must match pace, and the wrong tool for a sting that needs motion blur as a cut.

How it works

Fluid head, yaw only, horizon level, feathered stop on a composed end frame. Keep exposure in mind if you pan into a window.

Prompt a slow pan right from a locked tripod, fluid head rotation, level horizon, a continuous horizontal reveal.

When to use it

Same job as pan left, other direction. End on the story beat.

Concrete beat: a speaker finishes, the pan finds the listener who will decide. Do not overshoot and hunt.

Compared with similar shots

Pan Left is the mirrored yaw. A Dolly Right trucks the body.

A Whip Pan blurs this same axis on purpose. If the support slides, you left the pan family.

Pan LeftConnect two things in one geography without moving the support.

Whip PanTransition, punchline, or sudden attention shift.

Slow Zoom InUse to raise pressure without changing geography. The world stays put; attention closes.

In film

There Will Be Blood turns across interiors and landscapes to bind oil, prayer, and land in one station. The Rules of the Game uses fluid pans through the chateau so class and hunting share deep space.

Grammar of the turn, not a layout to copy.

Prompt it

Slow pan right from a locked tripod across [Subject], fluid head rotation, level horizon, a continuous horizontal reveal. For motion: the camera pans right from a fixed tripod across [Subject].

Smooth horizontal rotation only.

Use in Video Generator

The camera pans right from a fixed tripod across [Subject]. Smooth horizontal rotation only.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Dolly Right or a Whip Pan that never resolves. The tell is parallax you did not want, or blur that never hard-stops.

The fix: locked sticks, yaw right, level horizon, clean settle.

Questions

What is Pan Right in film?

It is a rightward yaw of the camera on a fixed tripod, sweeping the view horizontally without moving the support.

Pan Right vs Dolly Right

Dolly right relocates the camera on an X axis. Pan right only rotates, so you look at a new part of the same place from the same spot.

When should I use Pan Right?

When the next fact is to the right and a turn is enough to connect it. Do not use it to fake a track along a street.

How do I prompt Pan Right for AI image or video?

Write fixed tripod, pan right, horizontal rotation only, level horizon, no body travel. Name the landing frame.

entries.title: Tilt Up
entries.text:
Tilt Up

Tilt shottilt downreveal tiltPanoramique vertical

A tilt up shot rotates the camera vertically around a fixed position, climbing from a lower composition to a higher one. The tripod does not rise; only pitch changes, so the viewpoint height stays the same.

Volume

Create this Tilt Up

Narrative function

Height, awe, or a face can be delayed until the last part of the image is shown. Ground evidence connects to its source.

Scale becomes a relationship because we are forced to look up from where we already stand. It is the wrong tool when the camera must actually climb: a tilt cannot gain a rooftop's true station.

If architecture must slide down the frame with parallax, you wanted a pedestal or a crane.

How it works

Set a stable pivot and compose the lower and upper frames. Manage exposure if the move includes a bright sky.

Distinguish a tilt from physically lifting the camera. Prompt a slow tilt up, rotation on the horizontal axis, from ground detail to face or from face to towering architecture.

When to use it

Use it to reveal height, awe, or a face last. Concrete beat: boots, then the rifle, then the face.

Do not use it as a fake crane that never leaves the sticks.

Compared with similar shots

A Crane Up and a Pedestal Up translate the camera through height, so parallax appears. A Tilt Down is the same pitch axis the other way.

A Low Angle may be a still end frame; tilt up is the motion that can arrive there.

Tilt DownLand on a person or object after establishing scale above.

Crane UpEnd a scene, reveal a city, or turn a person into landscape.

Low AnglePower, monument, or intimidation.

In film

Psycho associates the motel with the house above it through vertical looking. Besieged connects a house's levels with vertical camera rotation.

Jurassic Park uses upward tilts so scale arrives as recognition. Confirm whether a given dinosaur reveal also dollies; the tilt is the pitch, not the track.

Besieged 1998Vertical camera movement connects the house’s different levels.

Psycho 1960Views associating the motel with the house above it.

Prompt it

Slow tilt up from [Subject], camera rotating on its horizontal axis, climbing from ground detail to face or from face to towering architecture. For motion: the camera tilts up from a fixed position, starting low on [Subject] and climbing vertically.

Use in Video Generator

Begin on a small muddy shoe at the foot of a massive stone monument. Slowly tilt upward from the same fixed position, revealing a child standing on a ledge high above. Maintain believable vertical lines, no crane rise, no zoom.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Crane Up or Pedestal Up. The tell is a changing eyeline height and sliding parallax of near objects.

The fix: freeze the tripod height, pitch up only, and let the top of the frame be the new fact.

Questions

What is Tilt Up in film?

It is a vertical rotation of a locked-off camera that pitches the lens upward, revealing higher parts of the same scene without lifting the support.

Tilt Up vs Crane Up

Crane up moves the camera through space, often backing away as it rises. Tilt up only turns on the head, so you look up from the same spot.

When should I use Tilt Up?

When height or a delayed face is the information and you are willing to stay at one station. Do not use it to fake a lift onto a roof.

How do I prompt Tilt Up for AI image or video?

Say fixed position, tilt up, horizontal-axis rotation, no crane, no pedestal. Name the start (ground, hem, desk) and the end (face, tower, sky).

entries.title: Tilt Down
entries.text:
Tilt Down

Tilt shottilt upreveal tilt

A tilt-down rotates the camera vertically from a fixed position, starting higher and ending lower. It can drop from sky or architecture onto a person or object without moving the tripod.

Volume

Create this Tilt Down

Narrative function

The new fact is below: a body, a key, a grave, a child. Establishing scale above, then landing, keeps rank in the pitch of the head rather than in a descending crane.

It is the wrong tool when you must arrive from a map into a street with true height change. A tilt cannot lower the lens into a crowd; it can only look down at one.

How it works

Compose the high start and the low end. Control exposure as you leave the sky.

Keep the support still so the move stays pitch, not boom. Prompt a slow tilt down onto the subject, starting in sky or ceiling and descending to the figure, a measured vertical scan.

When to use it

Use it to land on a person or object after establishing scale above. Concrete beat: a ceiling fan, then the sleeper.

Do not use it when the camera itself must come down to eye height.

Compared with similar shots

A Tilt Up is the opposite pitch. A Crane Down translates through height and can keep walking after the descent.

A Pedestal Down lowers the whole camera with tilt unchanged. Tilt down looks down; it does not sit down.

Tilt UpReveal height, awe, or a face last.

Crane DownArrive from god-view into a person.

Slow Zoom InUse to raise pressure without changing geography. The world stays put; attention closes.

In film

Citizen Kane uses vertical looking so ceilings and power share a sentence. The Godfather lands from rooms onto faces and objects as rank.

These are pitch grammar, distinct from crane descents that change station.

Prompt it

Slow tilt down onto [Subject], starting in sky or ceiling and descending to the figure, a measured vertical scan. For motion: the camera tilts down from above onto [Subject], revealing the figure from head to environment.

Use in Video Generator

The camera tilts down from above onto [Subject], revealing the figure from head to environment.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Crane Down. The tell is the camera's eyeline dropping through floors, with parallax as objects rise in frame.

The fix: keep the sticks planted, pitch down, end on the lower fact.

Questions

What is Tilt Down in film?

It is a downward pitch of a camera that stays in one position, scanning from a higher composition to a lower one.

Tilt Down vs Crane Down

Crane down physically lowers (and often advances) the camera. Tilt down only rotates, so height of the lens stays put while the look drops.

When should I use Tilt Down?

When the story fact is below the current look and you do not need a new station. Do not use it to enter a street from the sky.

How do I prompt Tilt Down for AI image or video?

Write fixed camera, tilt down from sky or ceiling onto [Subject], no crane, no pedestal. Name the landing object.

entries.title: Whip Pan
entries.text:
Whip Pan

swish panflash panSwish-cut join

A whip pan pans so quickly that the image blurs into horizontal streaks, then snaps to a new composition. Two shots can be joined inside compatible directional motion blur, creating the impression of one fast reorientation.

Volume

Create this Whip Pan

Narrative function

The move is a transition, a punchline, or a sudden shift of attention. Energy transfers between spaces that may not even be adjacent.

An ordinary change of location can feel like a comic snap if the blur matches. It is the wrong tool for a readable pan across a mural, and the wrong tool if you need to see the travel.

If the landing is not sharp, the whip is only a smear.

How it works

Match blur direction, luminance, duration, and acceleration if you cut inside the blur. Design the sharp landing before generating the two sides.

Opposite pan directions or mismatched brightness expose the seam. Prompt a violent whip pan off the subject, horizontal motion blur streaking the world, then a snap resolve on the next beat.

When to use it

Use it as a transition, punchline, or sudden attention shift. Concrete beat: a look off, a blur, a new room already in progress.

Do not whip across information the audience must read.

Compared with similar shots

A Pan Left or Pan Right stays readable. A Whip Tilt is the same idea on the pitch axis.

A Crash Zoom In blurs radially by changing focal length, not by yaw. Whip pan is horizontal speed past recognition, then a hard stop.

Whip TiltVertical shock instead of a horizontal whip.

Crash Zoom InPunctuate a hit, a realization, or a comic sting.

Slow Zoom InUse to raise pressure without changing geography. The world stays put; attention closes.

In film

Shaun of the Dead compresses routine and travel with fast visual joins. Hot Fuzz accelerates exposition with whip-like moves.

Baby Driver and Whiplash time the blur to music and hits. Use the matched smear and the landing, not the playlist.

Shaun of the Dead 2004Fast visual transitions compress routine and travel.

Hot Fuzz 2007Whip-like moves and abrupt visual joins accelerate exposition.

Prompt it

Violent whip pan off [Subject], horizontal motion blur streaking the world into ribbons, then a snap resolve on the next beat. For motion: extremely fast whip pan away from [Subject], heavy horizontal motion blur, then a sharp stop.

Use in Video Generator

Generate A: a baker turns toward a ringing telephone and the camera whip-pans right into horizontal blur. Generate B: begin with the same rightward blur and land on a flour-covered delivery driver outside. Join at maximum blur. Keep motion direction and brightness compatible; no dissolve.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a fast Pan Right that never blurs, or a Crash Zoom In. The tell is readable detail in the middle, radial zoom blur, or a seam where blur directions disagree.

The fix: commit to unreadability in the middle, match the join, stop sharp.

Questions

What is Whip Pan in film?

It is a pan so fast that the frame becomes horizontal motion blur, often used to hide a cut or to sting a new composition.

Whip Pan vs Crash Zoom In

Crash zoom in changes focal length and blurs radially. Whip pan rotates the camera on yaw and blurs sideways, then resolves on a new aim.

When should I use Whip Pan?

When you need a snap of attention or an invisible join between two setups. Do not use it to show a landscape.

How do I prompt Whip Pan for AI image or video?

Demand extremely fast horizontal pan, heavy motion blur, then a sharp stop on a named landing. If used as a cut, match blur direction on both sides.

entries.title: Whip Tilt
entries.text:
Whip Tilt

A whip tilt is a violent, motion-blurred vertical rotation of the camera, then a hard stop. It is the up-or-down cousin of a whip pan: shock through speed, not through traveling the support.

Volume

Create this Whip Tilt

Narrative function

Vertical shock instead of a horizontal whip. A body hits the floor, a face is found in a tree, a sign slams down from sky.

The middle of the move should be unreadable on purpose. It is the wrong tool for a slow reveal of a tower, and the wrong tool if you needed the camera to fall with a body.

Blurred pitch is not a crane collapse.

How it works

Rotate on the horizontal axis past blur, then hard-stop on a composed frame. Match blur if you cut inside it.

Keep the tripod planted so you do not add a drop. Prompt a violent vertical whip tilt, the frame ripping up or down with motion blur, then a hard stop.

When to use it

Use it for vertical shock instead of a horizontal whip. Concrete beat: from a screaming mouth down onto the weapon that caused it.

Do not use it to measure a building.

Compared with similar shots

A Whip Pan blurs on yaw. A Tilt Up or Tilt Down stays readable on the same axis.

A Crash Zoom In is optical, not a head rotation. Whip tilt is pitch speed, then a stop.

Whip PanTransition, punchline, or sudden attention shift.

Tilt UpReveal height, awe, or a face last.

Slow Zoom InUse to raise pressure without changing geography. The world stays put; attention closes.

In film

Evil Dead throws the camera through violent vertical reorientations as shock grammar. Crank uses similar speed as body panic.

These are references for blur-and-stop, not for copying specific gags.

Prompt it

Violent vertical whip tilt across [Subject], the frame ripping up or down with motion blur, then a hard stop. For motion: extremely fast vertical whip tilt across [Subject] with motion blur, then a hard stop.

Use in Video Generator

Extremely fast vertical whip tilt across [Subject] with motion blur, then a hard stop.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Whip Pan or a fast Tilt Down that remains readable. The tell is horizontal streaks, or a clear building in the middle of the move.

The fix: vertical blur, planted support, sharp landing.

Questions

What is Whip Tilt in film?

It is a tilt so fast that the image streaks vertically, then a hard stop on a new high or low composition.

Whip Tilt vs Whip Pan

Whip pan blurs horizontally by yawing. Whip tilt blurs vertically by pitching. Both plant the support and hide the middle in speed.

When should I use Whip Tilt?

When the shock is above or below, not beside. Do not use it for a gentle height reveal.

How do I prompt Whip Tilt for AI image or video?

Write extremely fast vertical tilt, heavy motion blur, hard stop on a named end frame. Specify up or down. No crane travel.

entries.title: Pedestal Up
entries.text:
Pedestal Up

boom uppedestal down

A pedestal shot moves the entire camera vertically without changing its tilt. The lens rises on a column, eyeline climbs, and architecture slides down the frame while pitch stays constant.

Volume

Create this Pedestal Up

Narrative function

Height changes without the drama of a crane arc. You are still looking the same way, only from higher, so rank and horizon shift together.

It is a formal lift, useful when the camera must stay architecturally true. It is the wrong tool when you need to boom out over a crowd or ease back as you rise.

A pedestal does not draw an arc; a crane does.

How it works

Use a studio pedestal, a column, or a virtual Y-axis translate. Lock tilt and usually lock yaw.

The nodal point gains height, so you get vertical parallax: near objects drop faster than the far skyline. Prompt a pedestal up, camera rising vertically on a column with no tilt change, eyeline climbing.

When to use it

Use it to change height without the drama of a crane arc. Concrete beat: from a tabletop to the standing speaker, looking the same direction the whole way.

Do not add a tilt-up and call it a pedestal.

Compared with similar shots

A Crane Up arcs through space and often eases backward, changing X and Z as well as Y. A Tilt Up only pitches from a fixed height.

A Jib Shot is a short pivoting arm, so its path is an arc, not a column. Pedestal Down is the same column the other way.

Crane UpEnd a scene, reveal a city, or turn a person into landscape.

Pedestal DownReturn to human height after a high formal view.

Slow Zoom InUse to raise pressure without changing geography. The world stays put; attention closes.

In film

2001: A Space Odyssey treats vertical camera placement as spacecraft geometry rather than as a flourish. Studio multi-camera drama uses the pedestal column as the default lift.

Pair those as grammar for tilt-locked height, not as a look to clone.

Prompt it

Pedestal up on [Subject], camera rising vertically on a column with no tilt change, eyeline climbing, architecture sliding down the frame. For motion: the camera rises straight up on a pedestal, keeping the same tilt, lifting past [Subject].

Use in Video Generator

The camera rises straight up on a pedestal, keeping the same tilt, lifting past [Subject].

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Tilt Up or a Crane Up. The tell is a pitching horizon, or a backward boom that reveals a city.

The fix: straight Y travel, tilt locked, no arc.

Questions

What is Pedestal Up in film?

It is a straight vertical rise of the whole camera with tilt held constant, so you look from a higher station in the same direction.

Pedestal Up vs Crane Up

Crane up follows an arm's arc and often backs away. Pedestal up is a column: height only, pitch unchanged.

When should I use Pedestal Up?

When you need a clean height change and a stable horizon, often in architecture or studio blocking. Do not use it for a skyline reveal that requires boom-out.

How do I prompt Pedestal Up for AI image or video?

Say camera rises straight up on a pedestal, no tilt change, no crane arc. Name start height and end height.

entries.title: Pedestal Down
entries.text:
Pedestal Down

pedestal up

A pedestal down lowers the entire camera vertically without changing its tilt. The descent stays on one axis: a calm drop through the same look, not a nod and not a crane swoop.

Volume

Create this Pedestal Down

Narrative function

Return to human height after a high formal view, or sit the camera down to a child, a table, a wound. Because tilt is constant, the world does not bow; we simply stand lower in it.

It is the wrong tool when you must look down as you drop, or when the arm should swing over a railing. If pitch changes, you left the pedestal.

How it works

Translate on Y only. Keep tilt, and usually keep yaw.

Vertical parallax reverses the up-move: architecture climbs the frame. Prompt a pedestal down, camera lowering vertically, no tilt, a calm descent through the same axis.

When to use it

Use it to return to human height after a high formal view. Concrete beat: from a chandelier's height down to the couple, still looking along the ballroom, not down at the floor.

Do not tilt to keep them in frame; change height instead.

Compared with similar shots

A Crane Down can arc, advance, and even hand off to a walk. A Tilt Down pitches from a fixed height.

Pedestal Up is the opposite column. Pedestal down sits the camera down while it keeps looking the same way.

Crane DownArrive from god-view into a person.

Pedestal UpChange height without the drama of a crane arc.

Slow Zoom InUse to raise pressure without changing geography. The world stays put; attention closes.

In film

Barry Lyndon favors formal, measured height and locked geometry over swooping arms. 2001: A Space Odyssey again treats vertical station as a physical fact of the set.

Use them as tilt-locked descent grammar.

Prompt it

Pedestal down on [Subject], camera lowering vertically, no tilt, a calm descent through the same axis. For motion: the camera lowers straight down on a pedestal, keeping tilt constant, settling onto [Subject].

Use in Video Generator

The camera lowers straight down on a pedestal, keeping tilt constant, settling onto [Subject].

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Tilt Down or Crane Down. The tell is a nodding horizon or a curved path over furniture.

The fix: straight drop, tilt frozen, end at the new eyeline.

Questions

What is Pedestal Down in film?

It is a straight vertical lowering of the camera with tilt unchanged, so the lens occupies a lower station without nodding.

Pedestal Down vs Crane Down

Crane down travels on an arm and often changes angle as it arrives. Pedestal down is a column drop: same pitch, new height.

When should I use Pedestal Down?

When rank or scale should change by sitting the camera down, not by looking down. Do not use it to dive at a face from a rooftop.

How do I prompt Pedestal Down for AI image or video?

Write camera lowers straight down on a pedestal, tilt constant, no arc. Name the start height and the settle.

entries.title: Crane Up
entries.text:
Crane Up

jib upboom up revealRise and revealGrue ascendante

A crane shot lifts the camera on a jib or Technocrane, often easing backward at the same time, so the frame climbs from a human scale into a wider view of the location. Height change is the point, and a little boom-out keeps the subject from sliding off the bottom of the frame.

Volume

Create this Crane Up

Narrative function

A crane-up starts at human height and leaves it. The person stays in frame, then the rooftops, then the city.

By the end, the figure is one dark coat in a much larger night. Use it when the scene needs to end, or when a private moment has to admit the world that contains it.

A tilt up only changes the angle. A crane changes the map.

Do not use it as decoration on every wide. If nothing new appears as the camera climbs, the move is empty.

How it works

The operator rides or remote-heads a crane. The arm can be a few feet (a jib) or tens of feet (a Technocrane).

Keep a foreground anchor visible during the rise so the newly revealed scale has a reference. Prompt crane up and slightly back, name the start (shoulder height, waist, close-up), and name the reveal (rooftops, canyon, overpass).

If you only write camera goes up, you often get a tilt or a cheap zoom.

When to use it

Use it to end a scene, reveal a city, or turn a person into landscape. Concrete beat: a woman on a wet roof, then the square below takes the frame.

Do not crane up if the last frame shows nothing the first frame did not already imply.

Compared with similar shots

A Tilt Up rotates on a fixed tripod. A Jib Shot is the short-arm version of this family.

An Aerial Pullback continues until geography wins completely from helicopter or high-drone height. A Pull Out stays at eye height and only retreats.

Crane Down arrives at a face instead of leaving one.

Crane DownArrive from god-view into a person.

Aerial PullbackClose a chapter. Geography wins.

Pull OutShow the container around a feeling.

In film

The opening of Touch of Evil treats the crane as a long sentence through a border town. The wounded-field pullaway in Gone with the Wind turns a person into a statistic of war.

La La Land lets hillside and dock cranes sit romance in a real city. The Player opens on studio-lot crane choreography.

Grammar, not frames to copy.

Gone with the Wind 1939Scarlett crosses the Atlanta station area as the view rises over wounded soldiers.

The Player 1992The opening studio-lot camera choreography.

Prompt it

Majestic crane up from [Subject], camera rising and easing backward on a Technocrane, the individual becoming one figure inside a vast environment, golden or blue-hour air, 35mm Signature Prime. For motion: the camera cranes smoothly upward and slightly backward from shoulder height, rising above [Subject] to reveal the true surrounding scale.

entries.title: Crane Down
entries.text:
Crane Down

A crane down shot lowers the camera on an arm from a high wide view into a human-scale frame. The world collapses from map to face because the lens occupies new heights, not because it merely nods.

Volume

Create this Crane Down

Narrative function

Arrive from a god-view into a person without resetting attention. What begins as an overview can become an intimate encounter in one path.

Some famous descents even hand off from crane to ground support and keep walking. It is the wrong tool when you only need to look down from a locked roof, or when a cut from aerial to close-up would be cleaner.

Do not assume every continuous-looking descent was achieved without a join.

How it works

Plan the high composition and the human landing. The arm descends, often moving forward as well, with a remote head keeping the subject framed.

If you add a support handoff, match direction, speed, height, and horizon at the transfer. Prompt a crane down from a high wide view into a closer frame, map collapsing to face.

entries.title: Crane Over
entries.text:
Crane Over

A crane-over lifts and arcs the camera on a jib or crane until it looks down on the scene from above. Height and angle change together in one move, turning the floor into a map.

Volume

Create this Crane Over

Narrative function

The shot turns a scene into a diagram without cutting. Bodies, tables, and streets become plan view because the arm has climbed and pitched over them.

It is not a still overhead: the audience rides the change of rank. It is the wrong tool when you already want a locked top-down, or when a simple crane-up should keep looking forward at a skyline.

If you never reach a downward angle, you only craned up.

How it works

Boom up and arc forward, remote head tilting down as the arm passes over the subject. End nearly nadir or at a steep high angle.

Watch for the subject being covered by the arm's shadow and for changing key as you face new windows. Prompt a crane over, arm rising and arcing forward until the camera looks nearly straight down.

When to use it

Use it to turn a scene into a map without cutting. Concrete beat: a dinner argument, then the table as a chessboard.

Do not crane over if the last frame is still a forward wide.

Compared with similar shots

A Crane Up typically keeps a forward look as it rises and eases back. An Overhead Top-Down can be a locked top-down with no ride.

A Jib Shot can do a small version of this arc over a table. Crane over is the continuous climb into downward view.

In film

The Untouchables uses crane height over the Union Station staircase so the action becomes a diagram of steps and bodies. Birdman rides theater space until floor plans and faces share one path.

Use the arc-into-down, not the period costumes.

The fix: one arm path that finishes steeply downward, subject still readable as a map.

Questions

What is Crane Over in film?

It is a crane move that rises and arcs until the camera looks down, combining a height change with a change of angle in one path.

Crane Over vs Crane Up

Crane up usually eases back while still looking across the world. Crane over continues until the view is downward and the floor becomes the picture.

When blocking should become a map without a cut. Do not use it if you wanted a skyline or a still overhead lock-off.

entries.title: Jib Shot
entries.text:
Jib Shot

A jib shot uses a short pivoting arm to raise, lower, or sweep the camera a few feet. It is a compact crane: small height change, often over a table, a walk, or a two-shot.

Volume

Create this Jib Shot

Narrative function

A few feet is enough. Music-video and dialogue coverage live here because the accent is intimate: over a drum kit, up from a plate, a gentle lift off a two-shot.

You are not turning a person into a city. It is the wrong tool for a skyline chapter-close, and the wrong tool if you needed a straight column with no arc.

If the arm is tens of feet, you are in Technocrane country.

How it works

Pivot a short arm from a base, remote or fluid head compensating so the subject stays composed. Typical travel is human-scale: table to standing, seated to slightly above.

Parallax is real but modest. Prompt a short jib move, compact crane arm lifting or sweeping a few feet, more intimate than a full Technocrane.

When to use it

Use it when a small height change is enough, especially music-video and dialogue coverage. Concrete beat: lift off a two-shot at a restaurant table so the room returns.

Do not jib if the story needed a city.

Compared with similar shots

A Crane Up is the large version that can make geography the subject. A Pedestal Up rises on a column with no arc.

A jib always draws a small radius. If you only nod, you wanted a Tilt Up.

Crane UpEnd a scene, reveal a city, or turn a person into landscape.

Pedestal UpChange height without the drama of a crane arc.

Slow Zoom InUse to raise pressure without changing geography. The world stays put; attention closes.

In film

La La Land uses small lifts as well as larger cranes; keep the jib examples at human height, over docks and rooms. Whiplash works close to the kit, where a short arm is an accent around sweat and sticks.

Grammar for a few feet of pivot.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a full Crane Up or a Pedestal Up. The tell is a skyline, or a perfectly vertical column with no arc.

The fix: name a short arm, a few feet of travel, and an intimate end frame.

Questions

What is Jib Shot in film?

It is a camera move on a short pivoting arm that raises, lowers, or sweeps a few feet, a compact member of the crane family.

Jib Shot vs Crane Up

Crane up can run tens of feet and turn a person into landscape. A jib is the small radius: table, kit, two-shot, a short lift.

When should I use Jib Shot?

When a small height or sweep accent is enough. Do not use it to close a film on a city.

entries.title: 360-Degree Orbit
entries.text:
360-Degree Orbit

circular trackingorbit shotOrbit 360360-degree shotpartial orbitArc shot

A 360-degree orbit shot circles the subject through a full turn, usually at a constant radius, always facing them. The background becomes a continuous ribbon while the person stays the center of interest.

Volume

Create this 360-Degree Orbit

Narrative function

Time can feel as if it collapsed around one kiss, one threat, or one product. Unlike a pan, the camera reveals different sides of the subject and changes their relation to every wall.

A full orbit calls attention to space itself; a partial arc can be quieter. It is the wrong tool when you only needed a quarter-turn to change a conversation axis, and the wrong tool if the subject is spinning on a turntable while the camera sits still.

Separate live-speed orbiting from bullet time, which also manipulates time.

How it works

Lay a circular path, pick a center, coordinate focus as distance breathes. Keep height even unless you also boom.

Do not zoom during the orbit unless you want a different technique. Prompt a full 360-degree orbit, constant radius, always facing the subject, background wrapping as a ribbon of light.

When to use it

Use it when a moment should close around one person: kiss, threat, or product hero. Concrete beat: a couple kisses while the room becomes a ribbon.

Do not also zoom, and do not let the subject rotate instead of the camera.

Compared with similar shots

Arc Left and Arc Right are partial orbits, often about 90 degrees, for axis change rather than spectacle. A Lazy Susan turns the object while the camera may stay put.

A pan never relocates the support. Orbit 360 is a full inspection on an azimuth circle.

Carlito's Way and American Beauty use live-speed orbits as trap or rapture. Grammar of the circle, not a costume to copy.

The fix: camera travels a circle, subject mostly still, background wrapping, constant radius.

Questions

What is 360-Degree Orbit in film?

It is a camera path that circles a subject all the way around, usually facing them at a steady distance, so every side and every background wall appears.

360-Degree Orbit vs Arc Shot

An arc is a partial curve, often a quarter-turn to change axis. A 360 orbit completes the circle and makes space itself the event.

entries.title: Arc Left
entries.text:
Arc Left

An arc left is a curved dolly that travels partway around the subject while staying aimed at them. The camera's axis on the conversation or room changes without a cut, usually about a quarter-orbit.

Volume

Create this Arc Left

Narrative function

You change who owns the background. A three-quarter face can become a profile, a window can replace a wall, the other half of a room can arrive.

The subject stays the center; the world slides. It is the wrong tool when you needed a full spin, a straight truck, or a pan from sticks.

If radius collapses, you accidentally pushed in.

How it works

Lay a curved track or walk a measured radius, always facing the figure. Keep distance roughly constant.

Ninety degrees is enough for most coverage. Prompt a 90-degree arc left around the subject, curved dolly, always facing the figure, background sliding.

When to use it

Use it to change the axis of a conversation or reveal the other half of a room. Concrete beat: from a frontal two-shot into a profile that discloses a listener in the doorway.

Do not complete 360 unless spectacle is the job.

Tracking Shot

A tracking shot moves with, beside, ahead of, or behind a moving subject, typically matching pace on a parallel path. The person supplies the motion; the camera keeps distance, height, and scale while foreground, mid-ground, and deep background peel.

Volume

Narrative function

Accompany a walker. The picture is not a postcard of a person; it is duration spent in their path.

Side-on tracking keeps cause, distance, and fatigue visible, which is why corridor fights and long walks live here. It is the wrong tool for a seated confession, and the wrong tool if you only panned from a locked tripod with a long lens.

If foreground does not slide, you did not track.

How it works

Use dolly, Steadicam, gimbal, or vehicle on a path parallel to the action. Match speed.

Hold a consistent distance and shoulder height unless the story changes rank. One direction.

Do not track a still interrogation.

A Follow Shot trails behind, using the back of the head as foreground. A Walk and Talk is tracking put to conversation coverage.

Steadicam is a support that often executes tracks. A Dolly Left can track a still line; tracking as a job is subject-locked travel.

entries.title: Follow Shot
entries.text:
Follow Shot

lead shotside-followchase shotwalk-and-talk

A follow shot trails a moving subject at a fixed offset, usually from behind. The back of the head becomes foreground and the world opens ahead, so pursuit, haunting, or arrival is felt as walking into space.

Volume

Create this Follow Shot

Narrative function

You are taken with them, not shown beside them. Doorways reveal themselves as they would to a stalker or a guardian.

The face is withheld, which can be predatory or intimate depending on distance and height. It is the wrong tool when the audience must read both faces of a conversation, and the wrong tool if the camera is bolted to the chest looking back at the actor.

Behind is a choice; body-mount is another.

How it works

Match movement through the space at a fixed offset. Steadicam, gimbal, or handheld can execute it; the grammar is the trailing station, not the vest.

Keep the head as a stable foreground mass. Prompt a follow shot behind the subject, camera trailing at a fixed offset, back of the head as foreground, the world opening ahead.

When to use it

Use it for pursuit, haunting, or walking someone into a room. Concrete beat: behind a child on a tricycle as the corridor keeps producing corners.

Do not follow if the scene is a two-hander that needs eyes.

Compared with similar shots

Tracking Shot often rides beside and shows the body's full action. Steadicam is a common support for follow.

A SnorriCam is mounted to the performer and faces them, so the face is pinned and the world sloshes. Follow looks at their back, not into their face from a chest rig.

Tracking ShotAccompany a walker. The shot is a journey, not a picture.

SteadicamLong connecting moves through architecture. Neither handheld nor dolly.

SnorriCamTrap the audience in a body that cannot get out.

In film

The Shining puts us behind Danny in the hotel so corners arrive as he arrives. Enter the Void uses trailing and floating follow as afterlife grammar.

Goodfellas' Copa entrance is a follow that becomes a social descent into a room. Path grammar, not a hotel to rebuild.

Prompt it

Use in Video Generator

The camera follows behind [Subject], matching their movement through the space.

The usual wrong cousin is a side Tracking Shot shot or a SnorriCam. The tell is a full profile, or a pinned face with a sliding world.

The fix: behind, fixed offset, head as foreground, space opening ahead.

Questions

What is Follow Shot in film?

It is a camera that trails a mover, usually from behind, matching their path so we enter rooms as they do.

entries.title: Steadicam
entries.text:
Steadicam

Steadicam is a mechanical stabilizing system using a sled, arm, and vest, so an operator can walk while the camera floats. The path can connect rooms with a smoothness that is neither handheld tremor nor dolly traction.

Volume

Create this Steadicam

Narrative function

Long connecting moves through architecture. Light temperatures shift as rooms change.

The operator is walking, so the camera can turn corners, climb stairs, and arrive in a new social weather without laying track through every door. It is the wrong tool when you want documentary shake, or when a straight corridor would be cleaner and cheaper on track.

It is also not a gimbal: the isolation comes from a mechanical arm and the operator's trained gait, not from motors alone.

How it works

Vest, spring arm, sled, and a balanced camera. The operator walks a rehearsed line; the camera is isolated from footfall.

You can still boom slightly with the arm. Prompt Steadicam floating with the subject through connected spaces, preternatural smoothness, operator walking, no footfall shake.

When to use it

Use it for long connecting moves through architecture, neither handheld nor dolly. Concrete beat: through a kitchen, down a stair, into a club, one path.

Do not Steadicam a lock-off that only needed sticks.

Compared with similar shots

A Gimbal Shot uses motorized electronic stabilization and is often run without a vest. Handheld keeps the operator's mass in the image as micro-tremor.

Tracking Shot is the job; Steadicam is a support that can execute tracks, follows, and Walk and Talk coverage. A Oner may be shot on Steadicam, but length of take is not the stabilizer.

Tracking ShotAccompany a walker. The shot is a journey, not a picture.

OnerThe scene is a ride.

In film

The Shining's corridor work is the textbook Steadicam walk. Goodfellas' Copa is a vest-and-arm descent through service spaces into a table.

Boogie Nights connects rooms as social circuits. Smooth path, human scale: that is the grammar.

What is Steadicam in film?

It is a mechanical stabilizer worn by an operator (vest, arm, sled) that lets the camera walk smoothly through spaces that track cannot easily enter.

Steadicam vs Gimbal Shot

Gimbal stabilization is motorized and often handheld without a vest. Steadicam isolates movement mechanically through an arm and trained operator gait.

When you need a long, smooth walk through doorways and rooms. Do not use it as a synonym for any moving shot.

entries.title: Handheld
entries.text:
Handheld

shaky camThe Children of Men car ambush

A handheld camera is operated from the body without a stabilizing vest or gimbal, so breathing, micro-shake, and mass stay in the frame. The image has the nerves of a person holding weight, not a track and not a motor.

Volume

Create this Handheld

Narrative function

Urgency, documentary contract, or a mind that cannot sit still. The operator is a body in the room, which can make escape routes and vulnerability tangible.

Used well, the shake is a result of attention and movement, not a plugin. It is the wrong tool for a formal lock-off, and the wrong tool if you add random shake to a tripod clip.

Do not describe a car ambush as simply a person with a Steadicam inside an ordinary car when the original was a designed interior path.

How it works

Hold the camera at the shoulder, chest, or under-slung. Let gait and breath exist; do not stabilize them out.

Exposure and focus are harder because the body is the head. Prompt handheld, breathing micro-shake, documentary immediacy, organic micro-tremors, no stabilization.

When to use it

Use it for urgency, documentary truth, or a mind that cannot sit still. Concrete beat: a raid through a crowd where the operator cannot get a clean view.

Do not handheld a still product on a table.

Compared with similar shots

Steadicam isolates footfall mechanically. A Gimbal Shot kills roll and high-frequency shake with motors.

Handheld keeps the operator's body in the frame's nerves. A Follow Shot can be handheld, but follow is a station, not a support.

entries.title: Gimbal Shot
entries.text:
Gimbal Shot

A gimbal shot uses motorized stabilization for smooth handheld or vehicle-mounted movement. Electronic inertia damps roll and high-frequency shake while a human still carries the camera, freer than a dolly and cleaner than raw handheld.

Volume

Create this Gimbal Shot

Narrative function

Run-and-gun smoothness without a Steadicam vest. Stairs, crowds, and vehicles become possible with a smaller footprint.

The image can feel slightly more weightless than a vest-and-arm, because motors, not a spring, do the isolation. It is the wrong tool when you want documentary tremor, or when a rehearsed vest walk through connected rooms is the grammar you actually mean.

Name the support; smoothness is not one thing.

How it works

A 3-axis motorized gimbal with IMU. The operator walks or rides; the horizon can be locked.

You can still boom and yaw with the handles. Prompt a gimbal move, electronically stabilized but still human-carried, smoother than handheld, freer than dolly.

When to use it

Use it for run-and-gun smoothness without a Steadicam vest. Concrete beat: down a stair, through a crowd, into a car, horizon mostly locked.

Do not gimbal a shot that should breathe as handheld.

Compared with similar shots

Steadicam is mechanical vest, arm, and sled. Handheld keeps tremor.

Gimbal is motors. All three can Follow Shot or track; the difference is how the support isolates the lens from the body.

SteadicamLong connecting moves through architecture. Neither handheld nor dolly.

In film

1917 mixes long connecting movement across supports; some passages read as gimbal-enabled freedom more than as classical vest work. Extraction uses motorized stabilization for action paths through crowds and vehicles.

Use the electronic lock and human carry, not a war to duplicate.

The fix: name gimbal, horizon hold, human-carried, no footfall bounce.

Questions

What is Gimbal Shot in film?

It is a camera move on a motorized stabilizer that damps shake while a person still carries or mounts the rig.

Gimbal Shot vs Steadicam

Steadicam isolates with a mechanical arm and vest. A gimbal isolates with motors. Both can be smooth; the mass and gait feel different.

When should I use Gimbal Shot?

When you need smooth walking or vehicle movement without laying track or wearing a vest. Do not use it as fake handheld energy.

entries.title: FPV Drone
entries.text:
FPV Drone

An FPV drone shot is first-person aerial flying: the camera banks, dives, and threads architecture at high speed. It is proximity and flight, a racing craft with a lens, not a slow crane and not a high establishing hover.

Volume

Create this FPV Drone

Narrative function

Impossible closeness at velocity. Windows, girders, and shoulders are obstacles in a flight path, not composition toys at a distance.

The horizon rolls because the craft banks. It is the wrong tool for a chapter-close aerial pullback, and the wrong tool for a dialogue two-shot.

If the drone flies like a tripod, you wanted a different aerial.

How it works

A small quad flown in first-person view, often with a bound or slightly stabilized camera. Banked turns, fast acceleration, edge motion blur, proximity to surfaces.

Name the route and the end composition. Prompt FPV drone racing past the subject, first-person flight, banking turns, proximity to architecture, motion blur on edges.

When to use it

Use it for impossible proximity and speed. Concrete beat: through a hangar, past a fuselage, out a door, into sky.

Do not FPV a still interview.

Compared with similar shots

An Aerial Pullback rises and recedes until geography wins, usually from helicopter or high drone with a level horizon. A Crash Zoom In is an optical snap from sticks, not a fly-by.

A Crane Up is an arm on the ground, tens of feet, not a missile path. FPV is 6DOF flight.

Crash Zoom InPunctuate a hit, a realization, or a comic sting.

Slow Zoom InUse to raise pressure without changing geography. The world stays put; attention closes.

In film

Top Gun: Maverick second-unit language made high-speed proximity a feature grammar. Music-video FPV popularized threading architecture and bodies at racing speeds.

Use the banked path and the near-miss, not a particular jet.

It is a first-person-view drone path that banks and threads space at speed, with the camera flying as a small aircraft rather than hovering as a crane.

FPV Drone vs Aerial Pullback

Aerial pullback recedes until a person is a mark on a map, usually level and high. FPV stays close, banks, and treats architecture as a course.
