When proximity and speed are the information. Do not use it to gently reveal a landscape.

entries.title: Aerial Pullback
entries.text:
Aerial Pullback

An aerial pullback rises and recedes until a person or building becomes a small mark in a landscape. The move hands the scene from a character to geography, from helicopter or high-drone height rather than from a ground crane.

Volume

Create this Aerial Pullback

Narrative function

Close a chapter. Geography wins.

The figure remains trackable long enough to prove continuity, then land, city, or army takes the frame. Timing decides whether the feeling is release or erasure.

It is the wrong tool at the start of a scene that still needs a face, and the wrong tool if a Technocrane's tens of feet would suffice. If you never leave human-scale air, you craned.

How it works

Helicopter, high drone, or virtual camera on a rising, receding path. Keep a readable anchor as scale changes.

Horizon can stay level. Prompt an aerial pullback, camera rising and receding until the figure is a speck in geography, helicopter or high drone grammar.

When to use it

Use it to close a chapter when geography must win. Concrete beat: a rider on a ridge becoming a mark in a desert.

Do not pull back if the last frame is still a medium-full of the same person.

Compared with similar shots

A Crane Up starts at human height on an arm and may only reveal a square. An Extreme Long Shot can be a still of that end frame.

An Aerial Push In is the reverse path, map to person. Aerial pullback is altitude plus retreat until land owns the picture.

Crane UpEnd a scene, reveal a city, or turn a person into landscape.

Extreme Long ShotScale is the emotion.

Slow Zoom InUse to raise pressure without changing geography. The world stays put; attention closes.

In film

Lawrence of Arabia lets desert scale erase and define a figure. The Lord of the Rings uses high pullbacks so companies become marks in ranges and plains.

Grammar of handing a scene to land, not a mountain to clone.

Questions

It is a high camera receding and rising until a person or building becomes small in a landscape, handing the scene to geography.

Aerial Pullback vs Crane Up

Crane up is an arm on the ground, often ending on a city block or a square. Aerial pullback works from helicopter or high-drone height until the map wins.

entries.text:
Aerial Push In

An aerial push in starts high and descends or tightens until a single figure reads in the map. It picks one human out of a city, crowd, or terrain from altitude.

Create this Aerial Push In

Narrative function

A system is shown first, then a person is found inside it. The audience is not asked to care before they see the grid, the convoy, or the desert that contains the body.

It is the wrong tool when you are already at eye height, and the wrong tool if a crane-down from a rooftop would reach the face. Altitude is the point of origin.

How it works

Begin in a true aerial, then descend and/or push while keeping orientation readable. Do not snap-zoom from a still map; translate.

Prompt an aerial push in from high altitude, descending and tightening from map to person.

When to use it

Use it to pick one human out of a system. Concrete beat: a border desert, then one unmarked police SUV, then a face in a window.

Do not start the move already on a close-up.

Compared with similar shots

Aerial Pullback is the reverse, person to map. Crane Down starts on an arm, usually from building height, not from thousands of feet.

An Establishing Shot may be the still first frame. Aerial push is the ride from map to someone.

Aerial PullbackClose a chapter. Geography wins.

Sicario finds figures inside desert and border infrastructure from the air. Children of Men uses high-to-ground pressure so a person is located inside a collapsing public space.

entries.title: Push In
entries.text:
Push In

A push in shot moves physically or virtually closer to the subject so size grows because the camera walks. It is a short pressure advance, often so gradual the audience feels the walls close before they notice motion.

Volume

Create this Push In

Narrative function

A thought lands. Do not rush it.

The job is the realization, the lie, the trap, not the display of a rig. Parallax still appears, even if the travel is only a meter, because the station point changes.

It is the wrong tool when you wanted optical compression from a locked body, and the wrong tool when you wanted a long track into a room as geography. If you add a second flourish, the thought is gone.

How it works

Dolly, slider, Steadicam, or virtual camera on the Z axis, usually from medium to medium close-up. Keep the lens fixed so the push is distance, not zoom.

Tiny parallax is the honesty. Prompt an imperceptibly slow push in, medium into medium close-up, walls closing before the motion is noticed.

When to use it

Use it when a thought lands and you should not rush it. Concrete beat: a listener understands they are caught, medium to MCU over 6 seconds.

Do not push in on every line.

Compared with similar shots

A Dolly In names the wheeled support and often travels farther, as geography. A Slow Zoom In never moves the camera, so there is no parallax.

Push in is the pressure beat: short, physical or virtual, tied to a thought. If the track is a room long, you are dollying.

Dolly InEnter a mind, a room, or a threat. Geography changes because the camera walks.

Slow Zoom InUse to raise pressure without changing geography. The world stays put; attention closes.

Slow Zoom OutReveal context, isolation, or a joke that was off-screen.

In film

The Silence of the Lambs uses slow physical approaches so conversations become traps. The Shining and There Will Be Blood let small advances register as mental weather.

Use the patience and the parallax, not a particular actor's blocking as a clone.

Questions

What is Push In in film?

It is a short, usually slow advance of the camera toward a subject so the frame tightens because the lens occupies a nearer station.

Push In vs Dolly In

Dolly in specifies a wheeled or tracked translation and can be a long geographic enter. Push in is the pressure job: often shorter, sometimes virtual, always tied to a thought landing.

When should I use Push In?

When a realization or trap should close the air around a face. Do not use it as a default on every close-up.

entries.text:
Pull Out

A pull out shot moves physically or virtually away from the subject so more environment enters around a person or detail. Intimacy widens into context without changing lenses.

Show the container around a feeling. The person remains while the world claims them.

A Slow Zoom Out discloses context without walking. Pull out is the generic physical or virtual retreat: the container appears because we backed up.

entries.title: Static Locked-Off
entries.text:
Static Locked-Off

locked offtripod shotSilence as tensionSparse sound field

A static locked-off shot plants the camera on a heavy tripod with zero camera movement. Composition, blocking, and duration do the work; the frame is a living picture that does not tour.

Volume

Create this Static Locked-Off

Narrative function

Trust blocking and duration. Movement would be noise.

Comedy, ritual, and dread all live here because the audience cannot be rescued by a pan when something enters, or fails to enter, the rectangle. It is the wrong tool when geography must be discovered in motion, and the wrong tool if you add a slider 'for life' and destroy the contract.

Silence of the head is a relationship to the action, not a frozen audio file.

How it works

Heavy sticks, locked head, level bubble, no touch after slate. Actors and air may move; the camera may not.

Prompt a perfectly static locked-off shot, heavy tripod, zero camera movement, composition doing all the work.

When to use it

Use it when blocking and duration should carry the beat and movement would be noise. Concrete beat: a domestic task held in a fixed composition until the task changes meaning.

Do not drift.

Compared with similar shots

A Tableau is a related still, often more presentational. A Long Take may be static or moving; length is not the lock-off.

Any dolly, pan, or zoom leaves this family. Static is zero camera path.

TableauHold the arrangement.

Long TakeDo not let the audience leave the room.

Slow Zoom InUse to raise pressure without changing geography. The world stays put; attention closes.

In film

Jeanne Dielman holds domestic tasks in fixed compositions. Tokyo Story lets rooms and sitting do the motion.

The Grand Budapest Hotel uses lock-offs as diagram. 2001: A Space Odyssey plants some spacecraft views as still geometry.

entries.title: Dolly Zoom
entries.text:
Dolly Zoom

vertigo effectzollytrombone shotContra-zoomTravelling contrarié

A dolly zoom combines camera movement and opposite zooming to preserve subject size while distorting perspective. It is not a zoom with a digital background stretch: translation and focal length work against each other.

Volume

Create this Dolly Zoom

Narrative function

The person appears fixed while the world becomes unreliable. Recognition, fear, or vertigo becomes a spatial event rather than merely a reaction close-up.

Use once; repeating it turns a contradiction into a trick. It is the wrong tool for a normal approach, and the wrong tool if subject size also changes.

If the crop simply grows, you zoomed. If the person grows and the room slides, you dollied.

The effect needs both, opposed.

How it works

Rehearse a dolly-in with zoom-out, or dolly-out with zoom-in. Match subject scale at both ends and coordinate focus.

Background perspective stretches or compresses while the chosen subject holds size. Prompt a dolly zoom: camera dollies while the lens counter-zooms so the figure stays the same size as the background warps.

When to use it

Use it for a realization that the ground is not stable, and use it once. Concrete beat: a seated watcher understands the water is no longer safe, body size holds, beach warps.

Do not use it as a stylish walk-up.

Compared with similar shots

A Dolly In changes subject size and perspective together. A Slow Zoom In changes size without walking.

Dolly zoom holds size and breaks perspective. That opposition is the whole technique.

Slow Zoom InUse to raise pressure without changing geography. The world stays put; attention closes.

Dolly InEnter a mind, a room, or a threat. Geography changes because the camera walks.

Slow Zoom OutReveal context, isolation, or a joke that was off-screen.

Vertigo looks down the bell-tower stairwell as space flexes. Jaws holds Brody's size on the beach while the background warps.

Goodfellas uses the diner talk near the end as a trap in stretched space. La Haine has a well-known rooftop cousin.

Geometry, not a face to copy.

It is a simultaneous dolly and opposite zoom that keeps a subject roughly the same size while the surrounding perspective stretches or compresses.

Dolly in walks closer and the person grows. Dolly zoom walks and counter-zooms so the person holds while the world becomes geometrically untrustworthy.

entries.title: Dutch Roll
entries.text:
Dutch Roll

continuous rollhorizon roll

A Dutch roll rotates the camera around the lens axis over time, so a level horizon becomes a canted one. Unease arrives as a move, not as a frozen Dutch still.

Volume

Create this Dutch Roll

Narrative function

The world itself tilts while we watch. Rank, gravity, and architecture go off their contract in duration rather than in a single locked cant.

You can stop on a Dutch angle, but the technique is the roll that got you there. It is the wrong tool when the floor is already the story (a listing ship), and the wrong tool if you needed a full continuous spin until up is gone.

A slow roll into a cant is not a revolving corridor.

How it works

Rotate around the optical axis (roll), usually from a locked nodal point. Keep pan and tilt still unless you combine on purpose.

End on a readable Dutch or return to level when the character finds the floor. Prompt a slow roll on the lens axis, horizon rotating from level into a Dutch angle.

When to use it

Use it for unease that arrives in time, not as a still cant. Concrete beat: a level street, then the horizon slowly dies as a fever starts.

Do not start already tilted if the arrival is the point.

Compared with similar shots

A Dutch Angle is a still cant. A Camera Roll continues until gravity is optional, or uses a rotating set.

Dutch roll is the timed transition on the roll axis into (or out of) a Dutch. Do not confuse it with terrain incline.

Dutch AngleThe world is off its axis. Do not use as decoration.

Camera RollGravity is optional.

Slow Zoom InUse to raise pressure without changing geography. The world stays put; attention closes.

In film

The Third Man is the still-cant grammar this move can arrive at: Vienna off its axis. Do the Right Thing lets living camera attitude, including roll and cant, sit in a hot street.

Use the moving horizon, not a postcard of a tilted doorway.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a locked Dutch Angle or a full Camera Roll. The tell is a still tilt from frame one, or a continuous spin past 45 degrees with no stop.

The fix: start level, roll on axis over time, end on a chosen cant.

Questions

What is Dutch Roll in film?

It is a camera roll around the lens axis over time, turning a level horizon into a Dutch angle (or the reverse) as a move.

Dutch Roll vs Dutch Angle

A Dutch angle is a still canted frame. Dutch roll is the motion that creates or releases that cant.

When should I use Dutch Roll?

When unease should arrive in duration. Do not use it if you only needed a locked cant, or a full gravity-free spin.

entries.title: Camera Roll
entries.text:
Camera Roll

Roll setRevolving room

A camera roll rotates the frame around the lens axis as if the world has lost its up, either by rolling the camera or by rotating a room around a weighted body. Gravity becomes optional, which is stronger than a small Dutch cant.

Volume

Create this Camera Roll

Narrative function

A familiar corridor can become an unstable physical system. The effect is strongest when bodies retain weight and surfaces remain solid: people walk on walls because the set or the camera has rewritten up.

It is the wrong tool for a 15-degree unease, and the wrong tool if you only tilted the image in post with no sense of mass. A tilted still is not a room physically rotating.

How it works

Either roll the camera continuously around the optical axis, or build a rotating set and keep the camera's relationship designed. Practical work needs engineered sets, restrained objects, and stunt coordination.

Prompt a full camera roll, the frame rotating as if the world has lost its up, or a rotating corridor with weighted bodies.

When to use it

Use it when gravity is optional. Concrete beat: a fight in a hotel corridor whose floor becomes a wall.

Do not roll a quiet dialogue that only needed a Dutch.

Compared with similar shots

A Dutch Roll is a slow transition into a cant. A Dutch Angle is frozen.

An 360-Degree Orbit circles a subject in yaw, changing azimuth, not rolling the horizon around the lens. Camera roll is about up and down swapping, not about walking around someone.

Dutch RollUnease that arrives in time, not as a still cant.

360-Degree OrbitTime collapses around one person: kiss, threat, or product hero.

Slow Zoom InUse to raise pressure without changing geography. The world stays put; attention closes.

In film

Inception's hotel corridor fight is a rotating set with weighted bodies. 2001: A Space Odyssey moves through circular spacecraft interiors so walking in a ring redefines down.

The fix: roll around the lens axis, or rotate the room, until up is no longer the top of the frame.

Questions

What is Camera Roll in film?

It is rotation around the lens axis (or a rotating set) so the horizon turns and up is no longer stable.

Camera Roll vs Dutch Roll

Dutch roll eases a level frame into a cant. Camera roll continues the idea until gravity is in question, sometimes with a revolving room rather than a small tilt.

When should I use Camera Roll?

When the story has unhooked gravity: spacecraft, dream architecture, a dance floor that forgets the floor. Do not use it as a default unease.

entries.title: Double Dolly
entries.text:
Double Dolly

Spike Lee floatDouble travelling

A double dolly shot moves performer and camera together on one rolling platform so their relative arrangement stays fixed. The actor appears to glide rather than walk: feet skating, weight transfer absent.

Volume

Create this Double Dolly

Narrative function

An interior state made external. Fate, dread, or transcendence carries the person through a hallway while the world slides.

It differs from a stabilized walk because normal stepping is missing on purpose. It is the wrong tool if the performer walks normally, and the wrong tool if only the camera dollies toward a planted actor.

Both must share the ride.

How it works

Conceal a platform (or a virtual equivalent) that carries actor and camera. Coordinate speed so background parallax is the only travel.

For generation, keep the feet still and the body upright while the environment passes. Prompt a double dolly: subject and camera share one rolling platform, figure gliding, feet skating.

When to use it

Use it when an interior state should be made external: the person is carried by an idea. Concrete beat: an armed figure glides down a hallway, feet not walking.

Do not use it as a fancy walk-and-talk.

Compared with similar shots

A Dolly In moves only the camera. Steadicam lets both walk, with normal gait.

Double dolly freezes the relationship and removes the walk. If the feet cycle, the float is gone.

Dolly InEnter a mind, a room, or a threat. Geography changes because the camera walks.

SteadicamLong connecting moves through architecture. Neither handheld nor dolly.

Slow Zoom InUse to raise pressure without changing geography. The world stays put; attention closes.

In film

Do the Right Thing is the float's home grammar. Malcolm X stylizes approach toward the assassination sequence.

BlacKkKlansman ends on an armed glide through a hallway. Inside Man uses a floating reaction after the apparent hostage killing.

Feet still, world passing: that is the tell.

What usually goes wrong

The fix: shared platform, feet not stepping, environment streaming, body upright.

Questions

What is Double Dolly in film?

It is a shot where actor and camera ride the same moving platform, so the person glides and the world slides while their size in frame stays oddly constant.

Double Dolly vs Steadicam

Steadicam follows a walking person. Double dolly carries both, suppressing the walk so the figure floats.

When should I use Double Dolly?

When a mental state should carry a body through space. Do not use it for ordinary corridor dialogue.

entries.title: SnorriCam
entries.text:
SnorriCam

body cam mountchest rigbody rigBody-cam facing the actor

A SnorriCam fixes the camera to the performer's body so the body remains stable relative to frame while the world moves. A rig points back at the wearer: the face stays pinned, the environment pitches around it.

Volume

Create this SnorriCam

Narrative function

Trap the audience in a body that cannot get out. Panic, intoxication, or dissociation becomes spatial because the person is locked to the image and the street will not sit still.

It is the wrong tool for a first-person view of what they see. A SnorriCam faces the wearer.

It is not a body-cam showing the world, and it is not a follow from behind.

How it works

Use a safely fitted lightweight body rig, or reproduce the relative motion in a virtual scene. Preserve tiny bodily movements without letting the face float independently of the torso.

Prompt a SnorriCam body-mounted on the subject, camera locked to the torso, face pinned, world sloshing behind.

When to use it

Use it to trap the audience in a body that cannot get out. Concrete beat: a panicked walk down a sidewalk, pupils steady in frame, storefronts shearing.

Do not use it as POV of the sidewalk.

Compared with similar shots

Point of View shows what they look at, from beside or as them. Handheld is an operator nearby, not bolted to the chest.

Locked-On glues the camera to a subject that may not be the wearer, often from outside a vehicle or a fall. SnorriCam is body-mounted and facing the actor.

Point of ViewForce identification. The audience is the character.

HandheldUrgency, documentary truth, or a mind that cannot sit still.

Slow Zoom InUse to raise pressure without changing geography. The world stays put; attention closes.

In film

Requiem for a Dream uses body-mounted shots during panic and disorientation. Pi destabilizes Max's movement through the city with a pinned face.

Mean Streets is part of the same body-rig family. Face stable, world not: that is the grammar.

The fix: camera on the body, pointed at the face, background shearing.

Questions

What is SnorriCam in film?

It is a camera rigged to the performer and aimed at them, so their face stays oddly stable while the environment moves around it.

SnorriCam vs Point of View

POV shows what the person sees. SnorriCam shows the person, locked to their torso, with the world unmoored behind them.

When panic, drugs, or dissociation should trap us in a body. Do not use it as a helmet-cam of the street.

entries.title: Locked-On
entries.text:
Locked-On

A locked-on shot keeps one object or face glued in frame while the world streams past, as if the camera were bolted to a vehicle, a fall, or a spinning set. The subject is the only stable point.

Volume

Create this Locked-On

Narrative function

One thing is the only law in a moving world. A steering wheel, a spinning astronaut, a driver's eyes: everything else is weather.

The constraint is rigidity to the subject, not a vest walking nearby. It is the wrong tool when you wanted a body-mounted face rig, and the wrong tool when a normal track should keep a walking distance.

Bolted is not following.

How it works

Mount to the subject, the vehicle, or match-move as if bolted. Distance and angle to the chosen object stay nearly constant; background parallax and rotation can be extreme.

Prompt a locked-on move, camera glued to one object or face, environment streaming past, as if bolted to a vehicle or a falling body.

When to use it

Use it when one thing is the only stable point in a moving world. Concrete beat: a close steering wheel and dash while the city smears the windows.

Do not use it for a sidewalk follow.

Compared with similar shots

A SnorriCam is a specific body-mount facing the actor. Tracking Shot holds distance to a mover but is not bolted; the relationship can breathe.

Locked-on is a rigid constraint: the camera and the chosen subject share a mount or a match-move as if they did.

entries.title: Walk and Talk
entries.text:
Walk and Talk

A walk and talk shot moves with speaking people, camera leading or flanking at medium, so information and geography travel together. Architecture flows while a moving two-shot (or a moving single with interruptions) carries the dialogue.

The job is coverage of conversation in motion, not a silent hunt. It is the wrong tool for a chase with no words, and the wrong tool for a seated interrogation.

If nobody is walking while talking, it is just a track.

Steadicam or gimbal, often leading, sometimes flanking. Hold a moving medium, shoulder height, leave headroom for doorways.

Recorders and extras must be blocked as part of the path. Prompt walk-and-talk tracking, camera leading or flanking at medium, architecture flowing, corridor energy.

Use it when information and geography must move together. Concrete beat: two people argue policy while threading a bullpen, never sitting.

Do not walk-and-talk a scene that wants a table.

Compared with similar shots

Tracking Shot is the broader travel job and may be silent action. A Follow Shot hides faces behind heads.

Steadicam is the usual support. Walk-and-talk is specifically dialogue plus path: West Wing grammar, not a hammer fight.

entries.title: Hyperlapse
entries.text:
Hyperlapse

A hyperlapse combines time-lapse with significant camera movement through space. Time is compressed while the camera advances in steps that assemble into a glide, so crowds and weather race along a real path.

Volume

Create this Hyperlapse

Narrative function

Duration becomes velocity. A walk that would take an afternoon becomes a few seconds, but unlike a locked time-lapse the station point travels: streets are traversed, not merely watched from one roof.

It is the wrong tool for real-time tracking, and the wrong tool for a tripod time-lapse of clouds over a still city. If the camera did not move between frames, it is not a hyperlapse.

How it works

Shoot discrete frames along a surveyed path (or simulate that in 3D), then play them at time-lapse rates. Align each frame so the move reads as a glide.

Crowds, traffic, and shadows should race. Prompt a hyperlapse toward or around the subject, time compressed, crowds and weather racing, camera advancing in steps that become a glide.

When to use it

Use it to show duration as velocity along a path. Concrete beat: approaching a monument while hours of foot traffic smear.

Do not hyperlapse a 6-second real-time conversation.

Compared with similar shots

Time-Lapse is often a locked or slowly panned interval. Tracking Shot is real-time travel.

Hyperlapse is both: interval shooting plus significant displacement. A Slider Shot interval on 100 centimeters is a tiny cousin, not a city traverse.

Time-LapseShow weather, construction, or a night becoming morning.

Tracking ShotAccompany a walker. The shot is a journey, not a picture.

Slow Zoom InUse to raise pressure without changing geography. The world stays put; attention closes.

In film

Koyaanisqatsi compresses traffic and weather into velocity, sometimes from moving viewpoints. Baraka and related city-interval work sit in the same family.

Music-video hyperlapse made the stepped camera path a popular grammar. Use time plus travel, not a particular skyline.

Prompt it

entries.title: Slider Shot
entries.text:
Slider Shot

A slider shot is a short, precise linear move on a compact rail, often 60 to 120 centimeters. It adds parallax to an interview, product, or lock-off without a full dolly track.

Volume

Create this Slider Shot

Narrative function

A full dolly is too much. A few centimeters of travel can prove the room has depth: a microphone in the foreground slides against a face, a bottle turns against a window.

The move is small on purpose. It is the wrong tool for a city block, and the wrong tool if you needed a curve around a product.

If the rail is meters long, you are dollying. If the path is a circle, you are orbiting.

How it works

Clamp a short rail, level it, choose a constant speed. Keep the move lateral or a tiny push; do not hide a zoom inside it.

Prompt a short slider move, 60 to 120 centimeters of lateral travel, product or interview parallax, precise and small.

When to use it

Use it when a full dolly is too much and a lock-off needs a little parallax. Concrete beat: an interview single with a lamp sliding in the foreground over 6 seconds.

Do not slider a chase.

Compared with similar shots

A Dolly Left is the same linear idea at room or street scale. An 360-Degree Orbit is curved and long.

A Push In may use a slider as the rail, but push in is the Z-axis thought; slider names the short linear tool. Slider is compact travel, not a path through architecture.

Dolly LeftSurvey a space or stay with a walker without turning the camera.

360-Degree OrbitTime collapses around one person: kiss, threat, or product hero.

Slow Zoom InUse to raise pressure without changing geography. The world stays put; attention closes.

In film

The grammar is commercial and interview more than a single famous scene: tabletop product films, documentary talking heads, small table moves inside features. Use the 60-to-120-centimeter parallax, not a particular ad to clone.

What is Slider Shot in film?

It is a short linear camera move on a compact rail, typically under about 120 centimeters, used to add small parallax to a still setup.

Slider Shot vs Dolly Left

Dolly left can travel a room or a street. A slider is the compact rail version: interview, product, a lamp sliding against a face.

When a lock-off feels dead and a full track would be too much. Do not use it as a substitute for covering a walk.

entries.title: Lazy Susan
entries.text:
Lazy Susan

A lazy susan shot rotates the subject on a motorized turntable while the camera stays put, or the camera circles at a fixed product-hero radius. Distance holds, so scale does not change, and the far wall barely shears if the disc is what turns.

Volume

Create this Lazy Susan

Narrative function

Use it to inspect. A coat, a bottle, a weapon, a figure treated as merchandise: every azimuth is offered without a cut.

Light should stay consistent so the object, not the room, is what changes. It is the wrong tool when geography matters.

If walls, extras, and lamps must slide to prove a living space, you want an orbit. A conversation, a chase, a blocked room: those need the camera to travel.

How it works

The classic rig is a motorized disc under the subject; the camera is locked on sticks at eye or product height, often 50 to 85mm so the silhouette stays clean. Alternate: a circular slider at constant radius with the subject locked.

Either way, nodal distance is constant. Prompt a slow turntable rotation or a camera circling at product-hero distance, one revolution or a 90-degree reveal, no zoom.

When to use it

Show an object or costume from every side: a dress on a dummy, a car on a cyc, a relic on glass. Do not use it for a talk; faces in dialogue do not need a spin.

Compared with similar shots

360-Degree Orbit walks the camera around a living space so walls and extras shear. A lazy susan keeps radius and usually the room still.

3D Rotation treats the figure as a virtual sculpture in computed space. An Arc is a partial circle that still faces a person in a real room.

360-Degree OrbitTime collapses around one person: kiss, threat, or product hero.

Slow Zoom InUse to raise pressure without changing geography. The world stays put; attention closes.

Slow Zoom OutReveal context, isolation, or a joke that was off-screen.

In film

Product films and music-video costume spins are the grammar: perfume turntables, album-cover rotations, a hero prop shown as a specimen. These are inspection uses, not a narrative street orbit.

Prompt it

Quote the move, not a mood. Still: Lazy-Susan rotation of [Subject] on a turntable while the camera stays put, or the camera circles a static product, commercial 360 hero.

Video: [Subject] rotates slowly as if on a turntable, or the camera circles at product-hero distance. Name the object, keep distance constant, forbid a zoom.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is an orbit. The tell: background sliding, a lamp shearing, the room turning.

The fix: lock the camera or lock the subject to a disc, keep radius constant, let only the object rotate.

Questions

What is Lazy Susan in film?

A lazy susan shot rotates the subject on a turntable with the camera locked, or circles the object at a fixed product-hero distance, so every side is shown without a change in scale.

Lazy Susan vs 360-Degree Orbit

An orbit moves the camera through a real room so parallax of walls and extras is the proof. A lazy susan keeps the radius and usually the background still; the object turns like a specimen.

When should I use Lazy Susan?

Use it to show a costume, product, or relic from every side. Skip it when the location has to act; then orbit or arc instead.

entries.title: Bolt Cam
entries.text:
Bolt Cam

A bolt cam hurls an ultra-high-speed camera along a crash rig toward an impact, then freezes. The punch is physical translation on a rail or pneumatic throw, not a change of focal length.

Volume

Create this Bolt Cam

Narrative function

The camera itself is the strike. Sports packages and music-video violence use it when contact has to be felt as a mass arriving, not as a tighter crop.

Near objects smear; the last frames can lock on the hit. Do not use it for a thought.

A realization wants a push or a crash zoom. A bolt cam that never hits anything is just a fast dolly with no grammar.

How it works

The body rides a crash rail, wire, or robotic throw aimed at a pad, a body, or a ball. Shutter is high; speed is tens of meters per second, then a hard stop or a programmed settle.

Parallax is violent because the nodal point really moves. Prompt a bolt-cam strike toward [Subject], ultra-high-speed camera on a crash rig, the lens hurled at an impact then freezing.

When to use it

Use it when impact is the beat: a punch, a kick, a crash test, a chorus hit. Do not use it as decoration on a wide that never meets a surface.

Compared with similar shots

A Crash Zoom In is optical: the camera stays put and focal length snaps. Bolt cam translates.

An FPV Drone flies and can miss; this is a aimed throw on a rig. A Robo Arm can repeat a path without the crash energy.

Crash Zoom InPunctuate a hit, a realization, or a comic sting.

FPV DroneImpossible proximity and speed. Not a cinematic crane; a missile with a lens.

Slow Zoom InUse to raise pressure without changing geography. The world stays put; attention closes.

In film

Sports impact packages and music-video crash units are the grammar. The shot is a stunt camera, not a dialogue tool.

Prompt it

Name the strike, the rig, and the freeze. Still: Bolt-cam strike toward [Subject], ultra-high-speed camera on a crash rig, the lens hurled at an impact then freezing, sports and music-video violence.

The usual wrong cousin is a crash zoom. The tell: no parallax, the background simply enlarges.

The fix: demand body travel on a crash rig, smear in the near plane, then a settle at contact.

Questions

What is Bolt Cam in film?

A bolt cam is an ultra-high-speed camera thrown on a crash rig toward an impact, then stopped. The lens physically travels; the hit is the end of the move.

Bolt Cam vs Crash Zoom In

A crash zoom changes focal length on a locked body. A bolt cam moves the camera through space at high speed, so near objects shear before the freeze.

When should I use Bolt Cam?

Use it when the camera is the punch: contact, a stunt, a chorus impact. Do not use it for a quiet close-up.

entries.title: Aerial
entries.text:
Aerial

aerial shotdrone establishingdrone widehelicopter shottopographic shotDrone-style follow

An aerial shot views a large area from a high flying camera so geography reads as a map, the figure small in land or city. Helicopter, drone, or a virtual path can carry it; altitude and a stable horizon are the facts.

Volume

Create this Aerial

Narrative function

Open a world. The high moving viewpoint relates a small traveler or vehicle to a broad environment.

It can follow, overtake, or abandon the subject so landscape becomes a force, not a painted backdrop. It is the wrong tool for a face.

If the beat is an eye-line or a whisper, come down. An aerial that never finds an anchor is weather footage.

How it works

Plan a safe helicopter, drone, or virtual path. Hold horizon stability and let foreground (trees, ridges, towers) pass to prove height.

Keep a visible subject anchor and avoid implausible jumps in altitude. Do not describe older helicopter footage as drone photography.

Prompt: Aerial of [Subject] from a high flying camera, geography readable as a map, scale first, the figure small in land or city.

When to use it

Use it to make the place bigger than the person: a car on a mountain road, a rider on a ridge, a city grid. Do not use it as a default establishing shot if a street-level wide already tells the map.

Compared with similar shots

Aerial Pullback specifically retreats until geography wins. Aerial Push In descends or drives in from the air toward a target.

FPV Drone flies through gaps as a subjective missile; aerial is a map, not a tunnel.

Aerial PullbackClose a chapter. Geography wins.

Aerial Push InPick one human out of a system.

FPV DroneImpossible proximity and speed. Not a cinematic crane; a missile with a lens.

In film

The Shining opens with an aerial pursuit of a car through mountain roads. Skyfall uses large-scale landscape and travel.

Lawrence of Arabia and Sicario treat desert and border as active ground, not scenery.

What is Aerial in film?

An aerial shot is a high flying view of a large area, with geography readable as a map and the person or vehicle small inside it.

Aerial is a high map of land or city. FPV is a piloted flight through space, often low and threaded, with the lens behaving like a missile rather than a survey.

Use it to open a world or to measure a person against land. Skip it when the scene is a face or a room.

entries.title: Arc
entries.text:
Arc

arc shot

An arc shot moves the camera around the subject along part of a circle while the lens stays aimed at them. A quarter or half orbit is enough: the axis of the scene changes without a cut, and the background slides.

Volume

Create this Arc

Narrative function

Use it to reorient. A booth, a kiss, a standoff can turn from front to profile to reverse without a cut, so the relationship is rewritten by parallax.

The subject can stay put; the world is what orbits. A full 360 is a different promise.

If you only need a new eyeline, a quarter circle is cleaner. If nobody's position in the room matters, an arc is empty decoration.

How it works

Lay track or a circular dolly, or walk a steadicam on a curve of constant radius, camera facing inward. Height usually holds (eye or chest).

Foreground posts, chairs, or extras should shear faster than the far wall. Prompt: Arc around [Subject], camera traveling a curve while facing them, background sliding, a quarter or half orbit.

When to use it

Change the axis without cutting: a table that becomes a two-shot, a reveal of who stands behind. Do not arc 180 degrees on every line; save the curve for a real change of power.

Compared with similar shots

Arc Left and Arc Right name the direction of travel. 360-Degree Orbit completes the circle and usually inspects a body in space.

A Pan only yaws from a fixed point, so the background does not parallax the same way.

Arc LeftChange the axis of a conversation or reveal the other half of a room.

Arc RightSame as arc left, other side.

360-Degree OrbitTime collapses around one person: kiss, threat, or product hero.

In film

Goodfellas often arcs around a booth or a table as alliances shift. Atonement uses curved travel inside longer takes to reorient a scene without a cut.

Use them as grammar for changing axis, not as frames to copy.

Prompt it

Name the curve, the facing, and how much of the circle. Still: Arc around [Subject], camera traveling a curve while facing them, background sliding, a quarter or half orbit.

Questions

What is Arc in film?

An arc shot travels the camera along part of a circle while facing the subject, so the background slides and the axis of the scene changes without a cut.

Arc vs 360-Degree Orbit

An arc is a quarter or half circle used to change axis. An orbit-360 completes the loop and treats the figure as something to walk around.

When should I use Arc?

Use it to reorient a scene without cutting: a table, a standoff, a reveal behind the subject. Do not use a full spin when a quarter will do.

entries.title: Choreo
entries.text:
Choreo

A choreographed camera times bodies and lens as one phrase of movement. The blocking is scored: steps, turns, and the support share a count, then the phrase ends.

Volume

Create this Choreo

Narrative function

The blocking is the music. Dance floors, musicals, and some fight halls need the camera to partner, not to report.

One phrase: a lift, a turn, a stop. Extra flourishes after the count read as a different shot.

It is the wrong tool for coverage. If you need an over-the-shoulder for a line, shoot the line.

Choreo that wanders off the dancers is a tour, not a duet.

How it works

Rehearse actors and camera as one system: steadicam, dolly, or jib, marks on the floor, a shared tempo. Height usually stays human.

Parallax of partners and set pieces should land on the beat. Prompt: Choreographed camera with [Subject], bodies and lens timed together, one phrase of movement, dance-floor blocking.

When to use it

Use it when a dance, a fight, or a walk is written as a single musical sentence. Do not use it to pretty-up a scene with no shared rhythm.

Compared with similar shots

Steadicam is the vest that can carry the phrase; it is a platform, not the idea. A Oner is about duration, a long take that may or may not be danced.

Choreo can be short if the count is short.

SteadicamLong connecting moves through architecture. Neither handheld nor dolly.

OnerThe scene is a ride.

Slow Zoom InUse to raise pressure without changing geography. The world stays put; attention closes.

In film

La La Land stages camera and dancers on one count. The Umbrellas of Cherbourg treats color, step, and lens as a shared phrase.

Use them as grammar for timed blocking.

Prompt it

Name the shared phrase and stop there. Still: Choreographed camera with [Subject], bodies and lens timed together, one phrase of movement, dance-floor blocking.

Video: Camera and [Subject] move as one choreography, a single phrase, no extra flourishes. Forbid a second unmotivated orbit after the stop.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a wandering steadicam. The tell: the camera keeps going after the bodies have finished the phrase.

The fix: one count, a shared stop, no extra travel.

Questions

What is Choreo in film?

Choreo is a camera that shares a count with the bodies: one phrase of movement, then a stop, as if the lens were a dance partner.

Choreo vs Steadicam

Steadicam is a stabilizer. Choreo is the idea that blocking and lens are timed together; it can ride a vest, a dolly, or a jib.

When should I use Choreo?

Use it for a dance, a fight, or a walk written as one musical sentence. Do not use it as default coverage.

entries.title: Conveyor
entries.text:
Conveyor

A conveyor camera treats the world as a belt: relentless lateral travel at constant speed, factory or infinite product-line geometry. The subject can stand still while the line delivers the next unit past the frame.

Volume

Create this Conveyor

Narrative function

Industry, process, no escape from the line. The shot says labor is a machine: bodies, boxes, or faces arrive and leave at one speed.

Comedy and paranoia both live here. It is the wrong tool for a walker you are meant to accompany.

If the person is choosing a path, truck or track with them. A conveyor that speeds up and slows with emotion is no longer a belt.

How it works

Lateral dolly, slider, or a treadmill-like set, constant velocity, often a wide or moderate-wide so units repeat. Foreground machinery should cross faster than the far wall.

Exposure can be industrial: hard practicals, green or sodium, no beauty key. Prompt: Conveyor move past [Subject], the world sliding on a belt, factory or infinite product line, relentless lateral travel.

When to use it

Use it for a factory, an assembly of faces, a process that will not stop. Do not use it beside a casual sidewalk chat.

Compared with similar shots

Trucking stays beside a walker; speed is human. Tracking Shot follows a chosen path.

Conveyor is the line that does not care. A Dolly can go any direction; this one is lateral and metronomic.

Tracking ShotAccompany a walker. The shot is a journey, not a picture.

TruckingStay beside a walker.

In film

Modern Times turns the factory into a belt the body cannot leave. The Parallax View uses industrial process and test-film geometry as a trap.

A conveyor camera is relentless lateral travel at constant speed, as if the world were a factory belt. The subject can be still while units keep arriving.

Conveyor vs Trucking

Trucking stays beside a person walking. Conveyor is industrial: one speed, repeating units, process without escape.

Dolly

Create this Dolly

Narrative function

Walk the camera. Change geography.

In, out, or beside: the point is that the support rolls, so space is proven by relative motion. A face can grow because you approached, not because the glass got longer.

A zoom is the wrong cousin when you need the room to be real. If you only need a tighter crop from sticks, zoom.

If the floor cannot take track, say so and use a vest or a crane instead of faking wheels.

Lay level track or dance the wheels on a floor. Height is set by the column (often eye or chest).

In and out ride the lens axis; a lateral truck is still a dolly. Keep the horizon honest.

Use it when the camera must walk: approach a face, leave a room, slide a corridor. Do not call a zoom a dolly.

Compared with similar shots

Dolly In and Dolly Out name the axis along the lens. Tracking Shot follows a moving subject.

A Zoom changes focal length with the body still, so there is no parallax. A Push In is often a vest or a looser approach; a dolly is wheels and a path.

The Shining rolls the camera through hotel geometry until space feels like a trap. Goodfellas uses wheeled and vest travel as continuous geography.

A dolly shot is a camera on a wheeled platform that translates through space, producing parallax. It is a physical path, not a zoom.

A zoom changes focal length from a locked body, so space flattens or opens without parallax. A dolly moves the camera, so near objects shear against far ones.

entries.title: Falling
entries.text:
Falling

A falling camera drops the lens through air with weight and wind, a body or viewpoint in free fall. Gravity is the path: the ground rises, air rushes, and the horizon may not stay polite.

Volume

Create this Falling

Narrative function

Gravity is the plot. A jump, a slip, a body leaving a roof: the shot lasts as long as the drop, often a few seconds, and the camera either falls with the subject or is the subject.

A crane down is not a fall. If the arm is supported and the speed is chosen, you have a boom, not weight.

A drone that eases down is also not this shot.

How it works

The camera is dropped, thrown, or flown on a path that accelerates downward: wire, descender, or a digital fall with the same acceleration. Wide or moderate-wide helps the ground grow.

entries.title: Fixed Cam
entries.text:
Fixed Cam

locked camera

A fixed camera locks position and tilt so all motion belongs to the world, not the operator. The mount does not pan, tilt, or travel; blocking has to finish the shot.

Volume

Create this Fixed Cam

Narrative function

Trust blocking. A kitchen, a hallway, a stage: people enter, work, leave, and the frame stays a law.

Duration becomes visible because the camera refuses to help. It is the wrong tool when a look or a stand requires a reframe to keep power readable.

If you start drifting to be kind, you no longer have a fixed cam. You have a timid pan.

How it works

Sticks, a wall mount, or a hidden lock-off. Pick height (often eye or a formal chest) and a lens that holds the room (often 35 to 50mm).

Deep enough focus that action in more than one plane can be read. Prompt: Fixed camera on [Subject], locked position and tilt, all motion belonging to the world, not the operator.

When to use it

Use it when the scene is blocking: chores, a ritual, a joke that happens in the wide. Do not free the head to chase a line.

Compared with similar shots

Static Locked-Off is the locked-off shot as a catalog size of move (none). Tableau is a staging idea: a composed field to be read as a picture.

Fixed cam is the camera-movement rule: the support does not participate. A Pan that only adjusts a little is already a different contract.

A fixed camera is locked in position and tilt. People and weather may move; the operator does not.

Tableau is a staging idea, a picture to be read. Fixed cam is the mechanical rule that the support does not pan, tilt, or travel. They often meet, but they are not the same word.

entries.title: Omnidirectional
entries.text:
Omnidirectional

360 video

Omnidirectional capture uses a 360 camera to record spherical space, so the viewer can look any way and there is no behind the camera. Off-screen ceases to exist as a hiding place.

Volume

Create this Omnidirectional

Narrative function

There is no behind the camera. Staging has to work in a sphere: crew, lights, and unfinished walls cannot hide at the operator's back.

The rectangle of cinema is a later crop, or the piece is truly VR. It is the wrong tool for classical coverage.

If you need off-screen as a threat, you need a directed frame with edges. A 360 file that is only ever viewed as a locked wide is a waste of the sphere.

How it works

A spherical rig or a pair of fisheyes stitched into an equirectangular world. Nodal point is a point in the room, not a rectangle.

Hide stands above or in set dressing; light has to live in the space. Prompt: Omnidirectional capture of [Subject], a world that can look every way, spherical space, no off-screen.

When to use it

Use it when the audience must be able to look anywhere: VR cinema, a room that is a trap in every direction. Do not use it as a fancy synonym for an orbit.

Compared with similar shots

360-Degree Orbit is a directed camera walking a circle; there is still off-screen. First-Person is a character's bodily view, usually a rectangle with hands.

Omnidirectional is a sphere. A Pan only yaws a limited angle from sticks.

360-Degree OrbitTime collapses around one person: kiss, threat, or product hero.

First-PersonThe audience is the character.

Omnidirectional capture records a sphere with a 360 camera, so the viewer can look any direction and nothing hides behind the operator.

Omnidirectional vs 360-Degree Orbit

An orbit-360 is a normal framed camera walking a circle. Omnidirectional is spherical capture with no off-screen.

entries.title: Pan
entries.text:
Pan

Pan shotslow panreveal pananticipatory panreactive pandelayed panFollow-and-settleInternal reframing

A pan shot rotates the camera horizontally around a fixed position, yaw on the vertical axis, feet planted. The support does not travel; the horizon should stay level as the frame sweeps the world.

Volume

Create this Pan

Narrative function

Connect two facts without moving the feet. A look, a landscape, a second person: the pan can reveal, follow, anticipate, or delay.

Small pans also reframe blocking so the camera stays almost invisible while power changes inside the frame. Unmotivated constant drifting weakens that change.

If nothing new is being connected, the pan is fidget. A truck or a dolly is the tool when you need parallax, not a swing.

How it works

Tripod or a locked remote head. Rotate on the vertical axis; keep the bubble level unless you mean a Dutch.

Speed is a choice: crawl, follow, or whip. Near objects smear at the edges on a fast pan; they do not shear as they would on a dolly.

Prompt: Pan across [Subject], camera rotating on its vertical axis from a fixed point, a horizontal sweep of the world.

When to use it

Use it to join two facts from one stance: a gun and a face, a window and a street, a speaker and a listener. Do not pan as a substitute for laying track.

Compared with similar shots

Pan Left and Pan Right name direction. A Whip Pan is the same axis at a speed that blurs the join.

A Tilt pitches on the other axis. A Dolly moves the body, so parallax appears.

Pan LeftConnect two things in one geography without moving the support.

Pan RightSame as pan left, other direction. End on the story beat.

Whip PanTransition, punchline, or sudden attention shift.

In film

The Searchers and There Will Be Blood sweep land from a planted stance. Eyes Wide Shut adjusts framing as dance partners move.

12 Angry Men reframes as the jury's alliances shift. Rear Window surveys a courtyard.

The Stendhal Syndrome uses a museum pan as a survey.

Plant the feet. Still: Pan across [Subject], camera rotating on its vertical axis from a fixed point, a horizontal sweep of the world.

The fix: lock the position, yaw only, keep the horizon level, and let the join be angular, not spatial.

Questions

What is Pan in film?

A pan rotates the camera horizontally from a fixed position. The feet stay put; the frame sweeps left or right to connect two facts.

Pan vs Dolly

A pan yaws on sticks, so distances do not change by travel. A dolly moves the camera through space and produces parallax.

When should I use Pan?

Use it to connect two facts without walking, or to reframe blocking. Do not use it as fake geography.

entries.title: Parallax
entries.text:
Parallax

Parallax cinematography is the relative apparent motion between near and far objects as the camera translates. Near things race, far things crawl; that speed difference is how the image proves the world has layers.

Volume

Create this Parallax

Narrative function

Prove the world has layers. A foreground railing, a mid-ground person, a far ridge: once the camera moves, their relative speeds cannot be faked by a zoom.

The shot is less a named rig than a test you apply to any travel. A zoom that claims depth will fail this test.

If you need a graphic flatten, zoom on purpose. If you need air and furniture, translate.

How it works

Any real translation works: dolly, tracking, arc, handheld, aerial. Place a near object in frame (post, glass, leaves).

The near plane should slide faster than the subject, the subject faster than the horizon. Prompt: Parallax around [Subject], near things racing, far things crawling, depth proven by relative speed.

When to use it

Use it when the room or land must feel thick: a walk past columns, a car past trees. Do not add fake 2.5D wobble to a still and call it a dolly.

Compared with similar shots

A Dolly is a wheeled translation that produces parallax. Tracking Shot produces it along a path.

A Zoom changes size without relative speed between planes. A Wiggle is a tiny stereo rock, parallax as a fidget, not a path.

DollyWalk the camera. Change geography.

Tracking ShotAccompany a walker. The shot is a journey, not a picture.

Slow Zoom InUse to raise pressure without changing geography. The world stays put; attention closes.

In film

The Tree of Life uses moving viewpoints so near nature shears against far sky. Gravity lets debris and faces disagree in speed as the camera translates.

Grammar: relative motion as proof of depth.

Prompt it

Name near, mid, and far, and make them disagree in speed. Still: Parallax around [Subject], near things racing, far things crawling, depth proven by relative speed.

What usually goes wrong

The fix: translate the camera and keep a near object in frame so it outruns the horizon.

Questions

What is Parallax in film?

Parallax is the relative apparent motion of near and far objects when the camera translates. Near planes slide faster; that difference proves depth.

Parallax vs Zoom

A zoom scales the image from a locked body, so planes do not shear. Parallax needs the camera to move through space.

When should I use Parallax?

Use it whenever travel should prove a thick world: columns, glass, trees. Do not fake it with a zoom.

entries.title: Pass Through
entries.text:
Pass Through

A camera pass through travels through a wall, a body, or a window as if matter were optional. The path is continuous: one side of the barrier, its thickness, then the next space, without a cut.

Volume

Create this Pass Through

Narrative function

Cut the building, not the film. A house can become a mechanism, a club a sequence of rooms, a body a door.

The audience is given omniscient access to geography. If you hide a cut on a passing truck, you have an invisible cut, not a pass-through.

The thickness of the wall or the flesh has to occupy the lens for a moment, or the cheat will read.

How it works

Build a 3D route or a set with a removable wall, then composite so objects keep thickness and shape. Lens behavior should stay coherent (no melting plaster).

Speed can ease through the barrier. Prompt: Pass-through of [Subject], the camera traveling through a wall, a body, a window as if matter were optional.

When to use it

Use it to enter the next room without a cut, or to treat a house as a machine. Do not use it as a default transition between any two shots.

Compared with similar shots

Flying Cam Transition is a flight that punches a threshold and lands in a new room as a designed join. Through Object In uses a named prop (keyhole, cup) and often changes scale.

Object Portal is the object-as-door idea. FPV Drone can thread a real opening; pass-through may ignore matter.

Slow Zoom InUse to raise pressure without changing geography. The world stays put; attention closes.

In film

Enter the Void flies through Tokyo rooms and bodies as if walls were optional. The Fight Club house tour treats a dwelling as a continuous mechanism.

Grammar: thickness, then the next space.

Prompt it

The fix: travel through the barrier and keep its shape during the passage.

Questions

What is Pass Through in film?

A pass-through sends the camera through a wall, body, or window as a continuous path, treating matter as optional while keeping the next space coherent.

Pass Through vs Through Object In

Pass-through uses architecture or a body as the barrier. Through-object-in enters via a named prop such as a keyhole or cup, often with a scale change.

Use it to change rooms without a cut, or to make a building feel like a mechanism. Do not use it as a cheap wipe.

entries.title: Tilt
entries.text:
Tilt

Tilt shottilt uptilt downreveal tilt

A tilt shot rotates the camera vertically around a fixed position, pitch on the horizontal axis, tripod planted. Height is revealed or hidden by angle, not by lifting the support.

Volume

Create this Tilt

Narrative function

Reveal height without traveling. A body from shoes to face, a building from door to roof, a dinosaur from ankle to skull: the facts are stacked on one vertical.

The feet do not move. A crane or a jib is the wrong tool only if you wanted parallax of a rising support.

If the foreground must slide as you climb, boom. If you only need to look up, tilt.

How it works

Tripod, fluid head, horizontal axis. Start and end on composed frames; do not overshoot into ceiling unless that is the gag.

A wide lens exaggerates vertical stretch; a longer lens keeps the stack calmer. Prompt: Tilt on [Subject], camera rotating on its horizontal axis, climbing or descending the world from a fixed point.

When to use it

Use it to reveal height from one stance: a statue, a tower, a person from ground to face. Do not tilt as a fake crane-up.

Compared with similar shots

Tilt Up and Tilt Down name direction. A Crane Up physically lifts the camera, so rooftops and streets change in parallax.

A Pedestal Up raises the support on a column without pitching. A Pan is the horizontal cousin.

Tilt UpReveal height, awe, or a face last.

In film

Jurassic Park tilts up bodies and gates to stack scale from a planted stance. Citizen Kane uses vertical swings and stacked compositions to turn height into power.

A tilt rotates the camera vertically from a fixed position. The tripod stays put; the frame climbs or drops to reveal height.

Tilt vs Crane Up

A tilt only changes angle. A crane physically moves the camera through space, so parallax appears and the map can change.

entries.title: Trucking
entries.text:
Trucking

truck

A trucking shot is a lateral dolly: the camera slides sideways with a walker, a sidewalk or corridor peeling by. Subject size holds; the world streams along the street axis.

Volume

Create this Trucking

Narrative function

Stay beside a walker. Talk, walk, and the city or the hallway becomes a moving set.

The camera is a polite companion, not a hunter in front and not a conveyor belt. If you lead from the front, you are tracking or following.

If the world is a factory that does not care, you are on a conveyor. Trucking is the side-on companion.

Track parallel to the walk, camera at eye or chest, often 35 to 50mm. Match speed to the stride.

Foreground (posts, extras, doorways) should shear; the far wall crawls. Prompt: Trucking with [Subject], lateral dolly, the camera sliding sideways, a sidewalk or corridor peeling by.

entries.title: Wandering
entries.text:
Wandering

A wandering camera drifts near the subject as curiosity, a search without a target yet. The move is not a motivated reframe to a known fact; looking itself is the action until something is found.

Volume

Create this Wandering

Narrative function

Looking is the action. Openings, parties, streets: the lens behaves like a guest who has not decided what matters.

Discovery is the point, not a pre-aimed hero. Once the camera knows the target and drives at it, the wandering is over.

A hunt is a track. A tour that never finds anything is also empty: curiosity still needs a world worth searching.

How it works

Steadicam or handheld, human height, no locked axis. Speed is uneven on purpose.

Let the frame glance off extras, corners, and unfinished business, then arrive. Prompt: Wandering camera near [Subject], unmotivated drift that becomes curiosity, a search without a target yet.

When to use it

Use it when the scene is a search: an opening that discovers a location, a camera that has not chosen a side. Do not wander through a scene whose power geography is already known.

Compared with similar shots

Handheld is a body and a shake; it can still be aimed. Steadicam is a float that can wander or can be a laser.

Wandering is the motive: discovery, not targeting. A Pan from sticks surveys from one point; wandering translates.

entries.title: Zoom
entries.text:
Zoom

zoom inzoom outslow zoomsnap zoom

A zoom shot changes focal length without moving the camera. Space flattens or opens with no parallax: near and far grow or shrink together because the nodal point stays put.

Volume

Create this Zoom

Narrative function

Change size without walking. Surveillance, emphasis, a punch: the glass does the work.

The background does not shear; it merely occupies more or less of the frame. If you need the room to be real, dolly.

The compound cousin is a dolly zoom, where travel and glass disagree on purpose. A zoom used as fake geography will flatten the set and give the cheat away.

How it works
